On 27 August 2020, feminist collectives gathered in Gijon demanding justice for the murder of a 43 years old woman in 2018.

On 29 May 2020, about 100 protesters, in both kayaks and onshore, gathered on Skrillinge beach, Middelfart to demonstrate against the construction of the Baltic Pipe gas pipeline and the government's investments in fossil fuels. Extinction Rebellion was in attendance.

On 21 February 2020, a group of social care and health worker members of Forsa who work for the National Council for the Blind (NCIB) staged a protest in Carlow town, Co. Carlow, about salary and labour conditions.

On 8 March 2023, between 800 (according to the police) and 2,000 (organizers) people gathered for a demonstration in Geneva on the occasion of International Women's Day, at the call of the Greve feministe collective, to demonstrate in favor of women's rights, equal pay, against sexual and sexist violence, and to oppose the patriarchy.

On 16 May 2023, an unknown number of students and activists staged a protest march through Gent, to demand the stepping down of Gent University's rector after the latter had announced budget cuts on sustainability policy.
On 12 December 2025, unionized miners gathered for a rally in Katowice, demanding higher financial benefits and better working conditions.

On 22 September 2021, in the morning, Focaccia Technical Institute students took to the streets in Calabrie street in the Fuorni neighborhood of Salerno (Salerno, Campania) to protest against local public transport companies and their alleged skipping of the bus stop in front of their school due to overcrowding, a situation they claimed worsened with coronavirus-induced capping on buses.

On 31 July 2025, residents protested in Tervel to apply public pressure against a planned wind-farm, just as the Tervel municipal council debated the project. The body agreed to seek a new environmental study and said it would refuse building permits until the residents' concerns about noise and bird migration are resolved.

On 5 April 2025, local citizens and those from surrounding villages and cities gathered in Bor, demanding accountability for the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse and observing 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign.

On 28 September 2021, students occupied their schools in Volos demanding increased coronavirus safety measures, more teaching and cleaning staff hirings in schools, no coronavirus tests for unvaccinated students, and they protested against the introduction of a minimum passing grade at university entrance exams among other issues. This was part of a student mobilization occupying 130 schools across the country called by the Coordinating Committee of Students.

On 28 February 2024, around 30 farmers drove on their tractors and stopped in multiple villages to lower the EU flag at half-mast between Trets and Rousset (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to protest stricter environmental norms restricting the use of pesticides, foreign imports, and bureaucratic constraints imposed by the EU.
On 8 March 2025, people demonstrated in Orebro to mark International Women's Day to show their solidarity and in support of women's rights.

On 20 June 2024, around 200 people from the Nalon area, called by the Platform for Public Healthcare (Plataforma por la Sanidad Publica), held a protest at the Valle del Nalon Hospital in Langreo (Asturias) against cuts on resources and medical staff envisaged at the hospital.
On 3 June 2020, around 2000 protesters gathered at City Hall in Belfast - South to support the Black Lives Matter movement and call for justice for George Floyd.
On 28 March 2025, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Oskarshamn, Kalmar, to draw attention to environmental issues and to demand action against climate change.

On 19 June 2025, representatives from the sector for people with disabilities, such as directors of sheltered workshops, day centers, adapted collective housing, and support services, gathered in front of the Parliament in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to call on politicians to take responsibility for the ongoing political impasse, highlighting that the sector's funding has stalled and essential decisions have been delayed for over a year, putting the future of services at risk, and that the lack of a functioning government prevents budget approvals and reforms, leaving hundreds of professionals unable to plan their work and thousands of people with disabilities facing uncertainty.

On 2 March 2025, almost 300 people, including PaP, PC, SGB, USB, XR, Besta Committee (Comitato Besta), COBAS, No Passante Assembly (Assemblea No Passante) and Climate Emergency Network (Rete emergenza climatica) affiliates, gathered in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to demonstrate against the increase in public transportation fares, accusing the mayor and region's President of implementing policies that make Bologna increasingly expensive and more oriented toward tourists rather than residents.
On 20 September 2021, members of an animal protection and defense organization gathered in front of the Parliament in Bern. They called for the abolishment of fur exportation.

On 21 September 2022, about 30 people, including PCF and EELV representatives, as well as a SUD delegate, gathered for a protest organized by the PCF at the sub-prefecture in Saint-Gaudens, against wars, notably the war in Ukraine and Yemen. The event was organized on the International Day of Peace.

On 6 February 2020, labour centres, unions and federations organised rallies and actions in Xanthi along with pensioners, the self-employed and farmers, to protest over proposed legislation on social insurance.
On 27 May 2022, citizens gathered in Cetinje in a support rally for the Ukrainian people. Citizens spread messages of peace, carried flags of Ukraine, and played the Ukrainian national anthem.

On 18 June 2022, a group of Catalan activists at the call of Desobediwncia Civil Catalunya installed 'border crossings' as a protest in Amer (Girona, Cataluna) at the entrance of the municipality proclaiming the town as a 'liberated territory' of the Catalan Republic.

On 1 September 2021, several tens of teachers and parents protested in Filiasi against the dismissal of a school principal. A county education inspector claimed that the protest was organized by an adviser of the mayor.
On 9 August 2023, around two dozen people protested in front of an apartment block in Habersaathstrasse in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) against its eviction and actions of the security guards.

On 24 October 2024, several dozen demonstrators clashed with police officers trying to evict around 50 unaccompanied underage migrants illgegally occupying the abandoned La Caravelle hotel in Toulouse (Occitanie). The demonstrators demanded decent housing for all homeless migrants.

On 20 January 2024, 40,000 people staged a protest in Bremen (Bremen), advocating against the AfD. The protest was prompted by concerns over a secret meeting between AfD representatives and extremists, discussing mass deportations of individuals with German citizenship and migrant background, leading to a heightened awareness and mobilization against right-wing ideologies in various cities.

On 21 May 2026, a large crowd of pro-Palestinian supporters rallied in central Athens and marched to the Israeli embassy (Attica, Athens) at the call of March to Gaza Greece to protest the detention and treatment of the Global Sumud Flotilla activists in Israel. The march was dynamic with protesters waving Palestinian flags; the main slogan was 'The Mediterranean does not belong to Israel'.

On 21 December 2023, around 400 people staged a protest in Altenkirchen (Rheinland-Pfalz), advocating against the transformation of the local hospital by the German Red Cross (DRK) into a regional health center, voicing concerns about potential job losses.

On 6 February 2024, farmers with 30 tractors participated in a motorcade between Viana and Mendavia (both Navarra). The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement, called by UdU on that day, against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector.
On 12 November 2022, around 300 people gathered in Villard-de-Lans, to denounce the multiplication of real estate and tourism projects that are densifying the Vercors plateau.

On 15 October 2024, LGBTQ+ associations and activists gathered near Madama Palace in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to protest against a bill that makes pregnancy for others a 'universal crime' (DDL Varchi). An M5S senator, a More Europe national deputy, an MEP (PD), the president of SI, as well as Arcigay, AGEDO, and Rainbow Families members took part in the protest.

On 29 April 2022, midwives of the Lilas maternity ward demonstrated in front of the Ministry of Health and Social Affairs in Paris at the call of the SUD union. They called for the safeguarding of their workplace, citing its importance in the defense of women's rights.
On 5 June 2022, around 20 demonstrators, including members of the Animalist Party and One Voice, demonstrated in Bordeaux on Animal Rights Day. They denounced animal suffering.

On 8 January 2023, citizens, summoned by PACMA, protested in Malaga (Andalucia) against the exclusion of hunting dogs from the Animal Protection Law, as well as to demand equal treatment for all animals.

On 4 February 2024, at the call of the Association of Vehicles Affected by Environmental Restrictions (Asociacion Vehiculos Afectados por Restricciones Medioambientales, AVARM), people held a protest in front of the Las Ventas bullring in Madrid - Salamanca (Madrid) against the prohibitions and restrictions of the Madrid 360 project and the mobility ordinance of the Madrid city council, which they claimed impacted drivers of older cars in the city.

On 4 August 2024, anti-racism campaigners from SUTR gathered in Lancaster (England). The event is part of a wave of gatherings and violence that occurred across the country and was triggered by the stabbing of children in Southport on 29 July 2024 and the disinformation campaign on social media about the suspect of the attack being a refugee.

On 25 May 2021, more than 70 Black Lives Matter supporters gathered in Bristol to hold a vigil to mark the first anniversary of the murder of George Floyd which sparked an international protest movement. A Green Party candidate was in attendance and addressed the crowd.

On 22 July 2025, a handful of Cypriot and Palestinian protesters, including members of AKEL, EDON and POGO, carrying banners and signs, such as 'Israel is Committing Genocide', rallied at the call of the Embassy of Palestine outside the embassy building in Nicosia during an all-day protest and hunger strike called 'End the Starvation of Gaza'. The numbers were small because the protesters were taking turns due to a heatwave. The protesters put up a sign in the courtyard reading 'State of Palestine - 420Km' as a reminder of the proximity of Gaza. They protested that opposing the Israeli government should not be grounds for labelling them anti-Semites. The Palestinian ambassador recited a poem and made statements to the media denouncing the silence of the international community, the killing of journalists and the Israeli PM's plans for a 'Greater Israel'.

On 13 January 2024, people demonstrated in Reykjavik to show support and solidarity with the people of Palestine amid the ongoing Israeli offensive in Gaza. The demonstrators also called on the Icelandic government to file a lawsuit against the State of Israel at the International Court of Justice for alleged war crimes committed in Gaza.

On 14 June 2023, activists from the Women's Strike movement gathered for a rally in Szczecin and many other cities across Poland and in abroad, protesting against the current strict anti-abortion law in the country. It was a reaction to yet another death of a pregnant woman that was denied abortion after a miscarriage and died as a result of subsequent medical problems.
On 7 February 2024, AUR members and supporters protested in Buzau, condemning the intention to set the same date for European elections and local elections.

On 21 May 2022, around 500 members of Fridays for Future demonstrated in Koln at the Roncalliplatz to demand more climate justice. Protesters also demanded climate protection after state elections recently took place.

On 11 June 2021, housing services staff, represented by the Unite the Union gathered outside Aberdeen City Council Headquarters in Aberdeen to protest against its proposals to merge the 'housing officer' and 'support officer' roles within the organisation which protesters claim will lead to lower pay and job losses.
On 18 November 2021, workers at a delivery company gathered in front of a supermarket in Lausanne to denounce their working conditions.

On 11 March 2025, in the morning, at the call of student and faculty unions, over 2,000 students, faculty, and staff, including members of AOB, gathered at Domplein in Utrecht (Utrecht), blocking traffic and staging a protest march through the city center. The protest was part of a nationwide strike against the government's planned 1.2 billion euro cuts to higher education. The demonstration ended around 13:00 after the march and additional speeches at Domplein.
On 27 March 2025, health workers held a protest at Hospital Virxe da Xunqueira in Cee (Galicia) to demand better safety measures after the recent series of aggressions against health workers.
On 2 April 2021, around 30 farmers and FDF activists staged a protest in Utrecht to demand a better revenue system for farmers and the introduction of the Farmer Friendly supermarket label.

On 15 May 2021, demonstrators marched in Stockholm to oppose coronavirus restrictions. The protesters were dispersed by police personnel as the number of participants exceeded the allowed gatherings limit. The demonstration was a part of the 'World Rally for Freedom' worldwide action against coronavirus related restrictions held on 15 May 2021.

On 28 June 2025, at the call of CP, farmers gathered and planted flowers in Figeac (Occitanie) to protest against the Duplomb Law, which aimed to legalize the use of certain previously banned pesticides, citing their potential environmental impact and health risks for both farmers and consumers.

On 3 August 2024, around 6,000 people gathered in Essen (Nordrhein-Westfalen), to protest for diversity and LGBTQ+ rights. The event was disrupted by approximately 20 young neo-Nazis who shouted right-wing slogans. The event remained peaceful.

On 17 September 2020, around 150 persons gathered in Vannes, at the call of the CGT, FSU, UNEF and SUD unions. They demonstrated for the 'rights of workers' following the coronavirus pandemic, as part of a national day of protests. They demanded a ban on staff cuts, more resources for public services and better working conditions.

On 18 March 2023, less than 20 people gathered outside Novotel in Ipswich to protest against the accommodation of refugees in the hotel. Also, more than 100 people outside the hotel for a counter-demonstration to show their support for refugees. Protestors were chanting and holding banners saying, 'refugees welcome here'.
On 24 March 2024, several hundred activists gathered for a pro-Palestine rally in Prague, criticizing ongoing military operations of Israel in the Gaza strip.
On 19 September 2020, thousands of people marched through Brighton city centre as part of the Black Lives Matter movement.

On 30 October 2022, around 300 people staged a protest on the Dam in Amsterdam to demand more rights for asylum seekers in the Netherlands and to denounce the ongoing asylum crisis in the Ter Apel asylum center. Different asylum seekers were present and gave speeches. The protest was an initiative of Platform Stop Racisme.

On 1 October 2025, at 5 pm, people, including students, researchers, and union representatives, gathered on Federal Square in Bern (Bern) for a national rally organized by VSS/UNES/USU to denounce federal budget cuts and rising tuition fees. The event was the culmination of a nationwide day of demonstrations held across several Swiss cities (coded as separate events). Participants warned that the planned reductions threatened teaching quality, research capacity, and equitable access to higher education.

On 13 July 2021, HVIM, Mi Hazank members and one MP, and Betyarsereg members protested outside the headquarters of an NGO in Budapest - XIII, condemning the alleged promotion and lobbying of LGBT ideology.

On 15 March 2024, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Umea, Vasterbotten, to draw attention to environmental issues and calling on the government to stop subsidizing the aviation industry due to its negative environmental effect.

On 29 December 2023, for a third consecutive day, Palestinian refugees demonstrated at Austurvollur square in Reykjavik urging the Icelandic government to aid in retrieving their family members from Gaza.

On 2 October 2025, in the morning, students blocked access to several high schools and universities in Rennes (Bretagne), opposing the government's draft 2026 budget, austerity measures, and the pension age increase, and calling for fair taxation and stronger public services. Around 300 people blocked access to Rennes 2 University. Police physically intervened to lift the blockade at Sciences Po Rennes and prevented high school students from blocking the entrance of the Jean-Mace high school, though protesters later organized a second blockade inside the school courtyard. The Rennes 2 campus was eventually evacuated after a fire of wooden pallets was reported, without direct police clearance. The events were part of a nationwide strike and demonstration day called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, FSU, and SUD to oppose the government's draft 2026 budget, denounce austerity measures, demand the repeal of the pension age increase, push for fairer taxation and conditions on corporate subsidies, and call for stronger public services and investment in a just ecological transition.

On 11 October 2023, activists from Extinction Rebellion staged a 'slow march' in Tampere calling for the protection of forests and for biodiversity. Police personnel were present to ensure the security of the event.

On 15 February 2026, a few hundred people protested in front of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Bem Jozsef Square in Budapest - II (District 2) against pollution at battery factories. Organized by Greenpeace, God-ERT, and other civil groups, demonstrators demanded accountability after revelations that the government knew about toxic exposure of workers at the Samsung plant in God.
On 27 January 2023, farmers of Thessaly moved more than 600 tractors, blocking village squares in Karditsa, to protest over rising production costs.

On 17 November 2024, demonstrators, including Russian community members, gathered in Stockholm to protest against the ongoing war in Ukraine and express their opposition to the regime of Vladimir Putin.

On 3 May 2026, hundreds of people gathered in Victory Square in Bucharest (Municipality of Bucharest) for a rally in support of the Prime Minister, two days before the vote on the motion of censure filed by the Social Democratic Party and the Alliance for the Union of Romanians. The Mayor of Bucharest and a National Liberal Party general councilor joined the demonstrators. Gendarmes with several intervention teams were deployed but no incidents were reported.

On 14 March 2025, residents and members of the municipal government held a protest in Vila Real (Vila Real) to demand the closure of the municipal landfill, citing environmental concerns, bad odors, and health risks. Protesters blocked the road leading to the landfill with vehicles to prevent trucks from entering and exiting. They denounced the continued operation of the landfill despite previous commitments to shut it down and accused the company Resinorte of exceeding its permitted waste capacity.

On 17 March 2021, couriers supported by their union participated in a motorcade in western Thessaloniki, including Ampelokipoi, Evosmos and Neapoli, driving to the Labour Center in central Thessaloniki. They protested for collective labor contracts, increased coronavirus safety measures, government support for the national health system, and against police violence among other issues.
On 5 June 2021, around 1,000 people took to the streets from Karlsplatz (Vienna - Wieden) to Heldenplatz (Vienna - Inner City) for a BLM protest in Vienna to protest against 'structural racism.'

On 10 November 2025, citizens gathered in Subotica to support a mother on hunger strike who lost her son following the collapse of the concrete canopy at the Novi Sad's railway station. She demands accountability for the tragedy, the release of detained students, and snap elections. SNS supporters counter-protested. A group of them blocked journalists from taking photographs, crumpled a reporter's press accreditation, and attempted to seize one of their phones.

On 10 May 2025, around 30 residents, including local politicians from the FvD and Party for Teylingen (Partij voor Teylingen) parties, gathered at the truck parking area on Teylingerdreef in Voorhout (Zuid-Holland) to protest against the planned establishment of an asylum seeker's center (AZCs) for eighty unaccompanied minor asylum seekers. The demonstrators expressed concerns about potential noise, nuisance, and safety issues for nearby neighborhoods.

On 1 May 2024, protesters, labor unions and workers gathered in front of the Prime Minister's office in Tirana to demand higher salaries and better working conditions on Labor Day. Albania has been suffering a continuous cost of living and inflationary crisis, which has particularly affected poorer and working class citizens.

On 6 June 2020, more than 300 people protested in Ingolstadt against racism and for human rights under the motto 'Black Lives Matter'. The protest was sparked by the killing of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.

On 11 May 2025, in the afternoon, thousands of people, including the Minister for Digital Transformation and Public Service (PSOE), the PSOE spokesperson for the Municipal Group, the SMR co-coordinator and Congressman, and individuals from the cultural, academic, political, and youth sectors, gathered in Callao Square in Madrid - Centro (Madrid) to call for greater European Union integration. Protesters advocated for the safeguarding of European values and social democracy, and emphasized the need to foster a sense of European belonging through education and civic engagement. The demonstration concluded with a performance of the 'Ode to Joy'.
On 11 September 2020, 4 students participated in a Fridays for Future protest in Tallinn, demanding 'decisive action' by governments in the face of climate change.

On 31 August 2024, at the call of the Alliance Against the Right, under the motto 'Whether in Thuringia or Hamburg: Not an inch for the AfD!', 750 people, including antifascists, gathered outside the AfD headquarters in Hamburg - Wandsbek (Hamburg), to protest against right-wing ideologies and in response to the electoral success of the AfD in Thuringen.

On 17 March 2024, members of the Ukrainian community demonstrated outside the Russian Embassy in Oslo to demand the immediate withdrawal of Russian troops from Ukraine and to oppose the ongoing presidential elections in Russia. The activists displayed a banner reading 'Terrorism Has Russian Citizenship'.

On 15 February 2022, dozens of students assembled at the VUB university headquarters in Brussels - Ixelles to denounce the approach of the university authorities towards claims of sexual intimidation of students by a professor.

On 11 June 2020, in the evening, around 100 police officers gathered in front of the police station of Bordeaux and dropped their handcuffs on the floor, at the call of unions. They protested against the declarations of the Minister of the Interior about implementing changes in the police arrest techniques that were made in response to a row of protests in the country against racism and police brutality.

On 28 September 2024, fifteen XR activists protested, seven of them climbing on the grounds of the Amercentrale power plant near Geertruidenberg (Noord-Brabant). The protest, organized by XR, Quit with Coal, 'WISE Netherlands' (WISE Nederland), and Committee Clean Air (Comite Schone Lucht), called for an end to emissions and the removal of emission rights, opposing the shift to biomass, which they considered greenwashing. The police physically removed the protesters at 16:00.

On 1 May 2022, the Communist party organized a gathering in Prague, criticizing the current capitalist system. About a dozen of counter-protesters gathered nearby, pointing to the crimes of the previous communist regime. They also noted the links of the party to Russia and declared their support to Ukraine.
On 15 July 2020, around 15 members of The Greens as well as residents and members of the SPD and the Pirate Party protested in Petershausen for the rights of the LGBT community.
On 18 December 2024, Extinction Rebellion staged a protest performance at a mall in Solna, Stockholm, to draw attention to overconsumption and to demand action against climate change.

On 23 October 2024, activists from Extinction Rebellion demonstrated in Kemi, Lappi, to oppose the opening of a new pulp mill in the area. The activists cited perceived negative environmental impact of the newly inaugurated pulp mill, highlighting its contribution to significant CO2 emissions and the effects of increased logging on Finland's carbon sinks and biodiversity.

On 9 May 2023, students staged a protest march from the High Street entrance of the University of the West of Scotland to Storie Street in Paisley, calling on more support during the cost-of-living crisis amid the financial problems of the students.

On 20 September 2024, around 100 educational workers, organized by the school union 'Preporod', protested in front of the Ministry of Education in Zagreb demanding an urgent beginning of negotiations on branch collective agreements.

On 17 March 2022, Save Hough End Fields protesters and residents gathered at the Manchester Town Hall extension building in Manchester during a planning committee meeting. They opposed the plans to extend Hough End Leisure Centre onto Hough End playing fields in a bit to preserve biodiversity and communal space.
On 14 April 2022, Nordic Resistance Movement activists gathered in Uddevalla to promote the movement's national socialist values and to oppose multiculturalism.

On 16 August 2025, anti-immigration protesters marched through Athlone (Westmeath) to oppose the establishment of a new accommodation center for international protection applicants (IPAS) in Lissywollen. Participants carried Irish Tricolors, placards, and banners with slogans such as 'Ireland Is Full,' 'Athlone Stands Together,' and 'No IPAS Centre Here'. Police forces were present to ensure public safety, and the protest passed off peacefully with no offences reported.

On 1 November 2020, demonstrators gathered in front of the City Hall in Odense against the decision of Poland's constitutional tribunal to impose further restrictions of abortion law. The demonstration was a part of a Europe-wide protest action in support of women's rights.

On 10 April 2022, Cypriots participated in an international action of solidarity with Mariupol and rallied outside a Limassol theater to show that Cyprus supports Ukraine. The protesters lit candles and wrote the word 'children' and sent solidarity messages with Ukraine.

On 8 March 2025, at the call of the Feminist Collective 69 (Collectif feministe 68), between 300 (according to the police) and more than 400 (according to the organizers) people, including trade unions, students and LDH gathered in Mulhouse (Grand Est). The event was part of a nationwide day of strikes and demonstrations called by CGT, CFDT, CFE-CGC, FSU, SUD, and UNSA, along with feminist associations, including NT, to coincide with International Women's Day, aimed at demanding improved working conditions, wage equality, and stronger measures to combat gender-based discrimination and violence.

On 17 February 2021, miners protested outside the Livezeni coal mine in Petrosani, demanding the payment of the delayed salaries and the clarification of the situation around the Hunedoara Energetic Complex.

On 12 September 2024, at the call of CGT, several dozen bus drivers gathered outside the Keolis headquarters in Rennes (Bretagne) to protest against what they deemed toxic management and demand better working conditions.
On 13 February 2022, around 900 people staged a protest in Brussels - Watermael-Boitsfort to denounce the imminent construction of social housing in their neighborhood.

On 28 November 2020, around 200 people demonstrated in Moulins against a national security bill that they condemned as a violation of freedom of information, protesters' rights, and media rights, as well as the implementation of global surveillance of citizens. They also denounced police violence.
On 2 March 2022, protesters gathered in Plovdiv to show their support for Ukraine in the ongoing conflict with Russia. The local Ukrainian community joined them as well.

On 1 October 2022, dozens of climate activists from Extinction Rebellion and Just Stop Oil marched through Westminster and blocked the traffic in London - Westminster to denounce the government's lack of action on climate change. This event was part of a six-week campaign to occupy Westminster in central London.

On 7 March 2025, students, teachers, and citizens blocked the main road in Valjevo, protesting against the political pressures directed at teachers as a consequence of their support for students' demands. Teachers voiced that they received reduced salaries for the previous month, despite being only a week in the blockade. The protesters also observed 15 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign in support of students demanding accountability for the loss of 15 lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the train station in Novi Sad. The protest marks the first day of the 'general strike', where workers and consumers across Serbia halted their activities to support the students' demands.

On 12 November 2022, 100 citizens and green activists, including Greenpeace and Attac delegates, demonstrated in Sete, at the call of the collective 'Bancs publics', Alternatiba, Attac, LDH, 51 and Greenpeace, to demand measures to combat climate change while the COP27 was held in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt. The demonstration took place as part of the Global Day of Action for Climate Justice
On 23 April 2021, activists affiliated with the Feminist Revolutionary Brigade gathered for a rally in Torun, protesting against alleged reduction of women's rights, including the right for abortion.

On 19 August 2025, teachers and the federations of education unions (FSLI, FSE 'Spiru Haret', Alma Mater) protested for the 13th day outside the Ministry of Education in Bucharest (Municipality of Bucharest), rejecting Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan's claim that teaching workloads had decreased in recent years. Protesters announced continued daily pickets at the ministry until early September and accused the government of trying to bankrupt public education and warned of teacher shortages due to austerity.
On 10 July 2025, activists from the Animal Save movement staged a protest performance in Stockholm to oppose animal rights violations, to promote animal welfare and plant-based diets.

On 19 August 2025, citizens gathered in front of the SNS offices in Cacak to show support for a student who was abused by the commander of the Unit for Security of Certain Persons and Objects (JZO: Jedinica za obezbedenje odredenih licnosti i objekata) during the protest on 15 August. Protesters also voiced their opposition to the ruling regime and reports of police brutality at recent protests.

On 12 April 2026, at the call of White Tide, around 3,800 people protested in Malaga (Andalucia) against the deterioration of the public healthcare system, demanding increased investment, improved staffing conditions, reduced waiting times, and opposing the perceived privatization of healthcare services.
On 3 December 2018, 2018 in Podgorica, Montenegro supporters of Democratic Front (DF) political party protested the arrest of two DF officials.

On 3 June 2021, Extinction Rebellion activists on hunger strike continued to gather in front of the Parliament of Sweden (Riksdag) in Stockholm to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.

On 17 April 2022, several SOR supporters and members protested outside the parliament building in Chisinau - Buiucani, demanding a stop to the war in Ukraine and condemning the performance of the government.
On 4 September 2024, around 100 people marched in Rovaniemi, Lappi, to oppose accommodation of tourists in residential buildings and calling for regulations for short-term rentals.

On 30 October 2024, around 80 people gathered at the pro-Palestine camp at the University in Dortmund (Nordrhein-Westfalen) for a virtual appearance by the well-known climate activist Greta Thunberg. Journalists faced obstruction while attempting to cover the event, with some being denied access and others being closely monitored by camp participants.

On 13 February 2024, about 50 farmers participated in a motorcade in Leon (Castilla y Leon), blocking the AP-66 road. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and of the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector.

On 23 January 2024, students blocked access to the university building in Nantes (Pays de la Loire) to protest against the government's immigration law, which they deemed xenophobic, unfair to migrants, and inspired by far-right ideas. The event took place ahead of the Constitutional Council's decision on the law's constitutionality, set to be issued on 25 January 2024.

On 25 January 2020, around two hundred protesters gathered in Lecco on the occasion of a demonstration organized by the Sardines Movement. They protested against Nazi-fascism since it was the day of remembrance. They also protested against homo-transphobia and the representatives of a local LGBT association gave a speech.
On 15 December 2020, people protested in Tirana against the recent police killing of Klodian Rasha, demanding the resignation of Albania's police chief Veliu.

On 21 February 2022, university staff belonging to the UCU gathered in Newcastle upon Tyne to strike in protest changes to the Universities Superannuation Scheme (USS) that members assert to cut pension payments by 35 per cent.

On 11 August 2025, around 40 Extinction Rebellion activists demonstrated during the Arendalsuka political event in Arendal, Agder, calling for a phase-out of fossil fuel operations and for climate issues to be addressed. Activists also displayed a Palestinian flag with the message 'Free Palestine'. Among those present were activists from Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Denmark.

On 27 March 2024, around 25 people, including PCF elected officials and members of the Kurdish community, gathered outside the Charles-de-Gaulle airport in Roissy-en-France (Ile-de-France) to demonstrate against the deportation of a Kurdish activist to Turkey, where they claimed he would be persecuted by the government. Around 20 people entered the airport and engaged in a brawl with members of airport security, before being separated by soldiers patrolling the terminal. Between three and five security agents were injured, one had to be hospitalized.

On 20 January 2026, on the 8th consecutive week of farmers' protests, following the 19 January meeting of farmers, livestock breeders, fishers and beekeepers with the Prime Minister, farmers started dismantling their nationwide roadblocks even though they were still dissatisfied. Farmers withdrew their tractors from a junction connecting multiple locations near Prosotsani.

On 15 February 2025, the Coalition for Democracy and Diversity, supported by several political parties, organized a protest at Schrannenplatz in Neuburg (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern), to show solidarity for democracy and diversity, with the participants voicing opposition to far-right ideology and activity.

On 25 October 2020, demonstrators, including ethnic Polish and women's rights activists, gathered in front of the City Hall in Copenhagen against the decision of Poland's constitutional tribunal to impose further restrictions of abortion law.
On 29 November 2023, farmers blocked the road with their tractors in Zupanja, voicing their dissatisfaction with the lack of governmental measures to assist them in dealing with swine influenza.

On 1 December 2020, 4 school monitors protested in Missillac for better working conditions. They called for more financial, human, and material resources especially during the coronavirus health crisis. They also mentioned better pay, permanent job contracts as well as recognition of their work.

On 13 November 2024, in the afternoon, several hundred people gathered for a protest in Henstedt-Ulzburg (Schleswig-Holstein) at the beginning of the AfD Schleswig-Holstein's regional party conference. The protest was organized by Henstedt-Ulzburg's Alliance for Democracy and Diversity (Henstedt-Ulzburger Bundnis fur Demokratie und Vielfalt), supported by unions and other initiatives. Participants, including Grannies Against the Right affiliates, opposed the AfD's presence and promoted democracy and diversity.
On 12 February 2021, an unknown number of people staged a protest at the Palace of Justice in Gent against the imminent demolition of the historical social housing quarter Bernadettewijk.

On 21 March 2021, nearly 1000 people, including singers, a Swiss teacher, protested in Annecy against coronavirus-related measures implemented by the government. They called for a more democratic system where they could have the choice to respect or not the measures. This happened in a context of a national movement called 'Freedom March'. They gathered without masks nor respected social-distancing. They were dressed for the occasion as if they were at the carnival.

On 17 January 2025, citizens protested in Nova Varos to show their support for students who have been occupying their faculties nationwide, demanding accountability for the loss of 15 lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the train station in Novi Sad, ultimately blaming corruption for this tragic event

On 5 March 2020, approximately 70 protesters, mainly farmers and rural people organized by the Green Party, conducted a mobile heavy-machinery based protest, driving from Eleja to Jelgava to protest plans to redistrict Latvia's provinces.

On 27 January 2026, residents of the Pantelej neighborhood in Nis began daily protests against the installation of a 5G mobile antenna in Vrsacka street. The protesters blocked the main boulevard in their neighborhood, citing health and environmental concerns. The group launched a petition demanding the removal of the equipment.
On 14 February 2021, an unknown number of people staged a protest in Braine-L'Alleud to demand more attention for children and youngsters during the coronavirus crisis.
On 26 August 2023, about 1000 LGBTQ+ activists gathered for a pride march in Kosice, demanding equal rights for people of all genders.

On 19 January 2024, activists from Extinction Rebellion blocked a mineral test drilling facility in the Viiankiaava protected area near Sodankyla, Lappi. The activists demanded that the work be stopped and banned by government due to its possible negative environmental impact.
On 3 May 2026, members of the Venezuelan community in Italy and Venezuelan nationals demonstrated in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to demand the freedom of more than 500 political prisoners.

On 10 April 2025, in the evening, demonstrators protested at the Gouda train station in Gouda (Zuid-Holland) in support of Palestine and against Israeli actions in Gaza, expressing their discontent with the Dutch cabinet's policy on Israel and its complicity in what they call the genocide in Gaza. The protest was part of a larger national action in eighteen Dutch cities.

On 6 June 2020, up to 1,300 people protested in Oldenburg against racism under the motto 'Black Lives Matter'. The protest was sparked by the killing of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.

On 11 April 2024, farmers kept protesting the border crossing point near Dolhobyczow, protesting against the so-called Green Deal requirements and against the ongoing imports of Ukrainian grains to the country.

On 26 January 2025, following leaked cell phone calls of the last moments of the victims of the Tempe rail disaster, protesters rallied in Naousa at the call of the association of the victims' families. The protesters demanded justice and accused the government of a cover-up. This was part of a large mobilization in more than 150 nationwide and international locations with the slogan 'I Have No Oxygen', the last words of one of the victims.

On 27 October 2020, hundreds of people, including local residents, shop, bar and restaurant owners, far right activists and ultra football supporters, took part in a sit-in in Montegrappa square in Varese to protest against the restrictions introduced by decree of the President of the Council of Ministers amidst a second wave of coronavirus infections and denounce the ensuing 'healthcare dictatorship'. The manifestation was reportedly peaceful, although some protesters carried a homophobic banner targeting the communication head of the Council Presidency.

On 1 October 2024, 500 people demonstrated in Albi (Occitanie). The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration day called by CGT, SUD, and FSU to demand better public service, protest against state budget cuts, and defend workers' rights. The protesters also criticized what they saw as an undemocratic rightward shift in the government, arguing that President Emmanuel Macron ignored the strong performance of the left in the legislative elections by appointing Michel Barnier (LR) as Prime Minister.
On 2 December 2020, families of two people who died of coronavirus protested in Bar, Montenegro, claiming the hospital in which they died was not equipped to care for patients.
On 4 July 2020, in the morning, nearly 300 persons gathered in Beynac-et-Cazenac. They protested in support to a project of road deviation that would improve tourism.

On 4 April 2023, activists, including current and previous members and MPs of the Smer party, gathered for a rally in Bratislava. They were criticizing the government and the president for a myriad of alleged failures and mistakes.

On 15 November 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of the movement Mothers for Peace (Mutter fur Frieden), dozens of mothers gathered on Friedens Square in Bonn (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to protest against the upcoming military service reform.

On 5 July 2021, citizens called by LGBT groups protested in Noia (A Coruna), demanding justice for the murder of a 24 years old young man who was beaten to death in A Coruna due to his sexual orientation. They protested against LGTBphobia.
On 12 June 2021, citizens called by the LAB trade union protested in Basauri to protest against homophobia. They denounced a recent attack against a man due to his sexual orientation.

On 20 April 2021, couriers and catering employees participated in a motorcade in Thessaloniki to protest against the government's proposed labor reforms. The protesters also demanded increased coronavirus safety measures ahead of the re-opening of the tourism and catering sectors, including coronavirus tests and to be prioritized for vaccination.

On 9 February 2024, farmers blocked with a few hundred machines a highway in Suchowola, protesting against what they see as a low state support to the national agriculture, including excessive bureaucracy and environmental restrictions, and against ongoing import of grains from Ukraine. Unionized truck drivers joined them in solidarity.
On 20 August 2022, members of the LGBT community and their supporters gathered in Rochester to take part in the annual Pride march and oppose discrimination against their community.
On 17 May 2023, activists gathered in Berlin - Neukolln, protesting against homophobia and transphobia and demanding equal rights for people of all genders.

On 8 March 2023, at the call of Be Our Voice RN, Literaturherbst Heidelberg and Frauen Leben Freiheit RN, around 900 people staged a protest march to Uniplatz in Heidelberg to show solidarity with women's rights protests in Iran following the death of Mahsa Amini, and demand equal rights for women. The protest was part of a series of global protests on International Women's Day.

On 25 May 2024, activists from the Nordic Resistance Movement demonstrated in various locations of Leksand, Dalarna, to promote the movement's national socialist values and oppose multiculturalism and migration.

Around 15 February 2025 (month of), solidarity protesters prevented the foreclosure of the home of a single mother in Patissia, Athens - Central Athens, for about 1,000 euros debt. This was the third attempt to evict the family, who managed to save their home.

On 29 October 2023, several hundred citizens and civil society representatives gathered in Stolac to oppose the Israeli government and the mass killing of civilians in Gaza. The protesters expressed solidarity with the innocent Palestinian victims.
On 18 March 2023, activists, including Coalition Against Racism members, gathered for a rally in Warsaw, protesting against racism and demanding higher solidarity with refugees coming to Poland.

On 31 May 2022, employees of Markas, the company managing cleaning services in AUSL public healthcare facilities, staged a demonstration in Reggio Emilia (Reggio nell'Emilia, Emilia-Romagna) to protest against 'paycheck shortages' and organizational shortcomings. CGIL, CISL and UIL took part in the demonstration.

On 20 December 2025, members of the Szikra Movement held a symbolic Christmas tree installation protest in front of an empty residential building at Kossuth Street 26 in Debrecen (Debreceni, Hajdu-Bihar), criticizing the city's housing policy, opposing the sale of municipal properties to private developers, and demanding construction of social housing to address the local housing crisis; a police investigation for mismanagement is ongoing regarding the property's sale.

On 21 February 2026, XR activists staged a protest outside a Nando's restaurant in Winchester (England) to highlight the environmental impact of intensive poultry farming on UK rivers. The protesters targeted the restaurant chain for its sourcing practices, claiming that factory farms supplying the company contributed to high levels of phosphate pollution in the River Wye through chicken manure runoff.

On 6 November 2022, Mediterranea Saving Humans activists protested in Venezia (Venezia, Veneto) against the newly appointed Minister of Internal Affairs who was in the city to attend a ceremony and to demand all shipwrecked migrants on board of a ship docked in Catania be disembarked.
On 16 November 2021, bus drivers demonstrated at the Central Station in Malmo to oppose poor working conditions, including long hour shifts and increased workload.

On 31 March 2022, around 30 people, including the LGBT community and AI members (specifically Queer Amnesty), demonstrated in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg), in St. Pauli, against discrimination against transgender people and for LGBT rights on the occasion of the International Transgender Day of Visibility.

On 11 April 2024, at the call of Canary Islands is exhausted platform (La plataforma Canarias se agota), people protested in Santa Cruz de Tenerife (Canarias) to demand an end to mass tourism. They yelled slogans such as 'Canarias isn't for sale', 'Corrupt politicians out of Canarias'.

On 17 February 2021, animal rights activists from the Animal Alliance movement gathered in front of a local grocery store in Copenhagen to oppose selling of broiler chicken and in support of animal rights.

On 9 May 2021, around 150 demonstrators gathered in Saint-Lo. They demanded actions to tackle the climate emergency and called for improvements in the 'Climate and Resilience' bill on global warming adopted by the French Parliament on 4 May.

On 30 June 2023, overnight, rioters set ablaze the Croix-Rousse police station and vandalized supermarkets and shops in Lyon. 21 rioters were arrested. The event was part of a national wave of riots and demonstrations denouncing police violence and demanding justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre on 27 June 2023.

On 20 November 2020, a group of Eurospin Tirrenica employees took part in a sit-in in front of their workplace in Vinci (Firenze, Toscana) to denounce their working conditions and the lack of protection received amidst a second wave of coronavirus infections. The demonstration was part of a day of protest against Eurospin Tirrenica in the Toscana region called and coordinated by CGIL and UIL.

On 15 June 2025, during nationwide demonstrations at the call of March to Gaza Greece, which was part of the international initiative Global March to Gaza, thousands of students, members of labor unions, the Palestinian community and members of civil society organizations and political parties rallied and marched in central Thessaloniki, passing by the United States consulate, shouting slogans in solidarity with the Palestinian people and demanding an end to Israel's attacks on Gaza. They also protested for the recognition of the state of Palestine and against Greece's deepening partnership with Israel.
On 23 February 2024, farmers protested around Cahul, demanding more government support and compensations for harvest losses.

On 2 July 2022, around 20 people from the Aterra movement, some in pajamas as requested by the organization, participated in a protest at the Santa Apolonia train station, in Lisbon (Lisboa), to demand the return of train connections to Madrid (Spain) and Hendaye (France).

On 24 November 2020, hundreds of persons gathered at the Jean-Jaures square in Toulouse. They called for the removal of article 24 of the 'comprehensive security' bill, voted that day, and denounced its potential infringement of the principle of freedom of information, especially on reporting on police brutality. The article criminalizes the dissemination of images with personal identifiers of a police or military officer, with the aim of affecting his or her physical or psychological integrity.
On 11 May 2024, around 50 people staged a demonstration in front of the town hall in Amiens (Hauts-de-France) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and demand a ceasefire.

On 28 January 2022, about 20 students gathered, at the call of UdS, in Italia square, outside the Provincial School Office, in Pavia (Pavia, Lombardia) to demand more safety and less labor precarity for students and denounce the country's work-study program following the death, of a work accident, of an 18-year-old student from Udine while doing an internship in Lauzacco on 21 January 2022. The event was part of a national day of protest called by students' unions.

On 27 January 2021, a group of bar and restaurant owners advocating the 'I Open' (#IoApro) campaign gathered in front of the Sardegna Region's tourism department office in Cagliari (Cagliari, Sardegna) to demand concrete relief measures to their category from regional authorities due to coronavirus restrictions affecting their businesses.

On 8 April 2021, around 100 people, including civil servants, teachers, school assistants for students with disabilities, employees of the medical-social, metal industry, and education sector, protested in Chateauroux at the call of unions (CGT, SNES-FSU) to demand more recognition and better pay. They protested against the government's policies that are allegedly causing the decline of the public sector. Social workers called for a monthly salary increase that hospital health workers have been granted by the Segur agreements.

On 12 July 2025, nearly 1,500 people, including members of OGBL and the Minister for Gender Equality and Diversity (DP), took part in a Pride March through Esch-sur-Alzette (Esch-sur-Alzette) to express support and solidarity for the queer community. Protesters opposed attacks on the rights of LGBTQ+ communities. The event was organized by Rosa Letzebuerg.

On 15 April 2021, dozens of persons called by antifascist movements gathered in Abadino (Bizkaia) to complain over the 'violent forced eviction' of a group of squatters in the Zelaieta district early in the morning. The eviction was undertaken by workers of the 'De-squat' company who the property's owner hired. Police officers clashed with rioters while preventing the re-occupation of the building. One person was arrested.

On 23 March 2022, citizens gathered in Cetinje in a support rally for the Ukrainian people. Citizens paid special tribute to Mariupol, comparing the Russian devastation of the city with the Nazi devastation of Guernica in 1937. Those gathered also called for donations to Ukraine.
On 4 July 2020, a protest to call for action to assist the Palestinian population in their fight for rights was held in Dublin. It was organised by the Irish Palestine Solidarity Campaign.

On 1 February 2024, around 13000 people demonstrated at the Senate Square in Helsinki to support the ongoing nationwide strike and against the social security cuts and labor reforms by the government of Prime Minister Petteri Orpo. The events was organised by the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) and the Finnish Confederation of Professionals (STTK).

On 15 February 2026, at around 4 pm, a large group of residents, women, and activists gathered at Santi Apostoli Square in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to demonstrate against a law proposal they considered to be lacking and ineffective, namely the DDL Buongiorno, aiming to regulate linked to sexual violence and consensual sex. The demonstration was held as part of a national wave of protests against the law proposal, sexual violence, and violence against women.

On 23 August 2024, around 200 people gathered in Erlangen (Bayern) to protest against far-right activities and racism. The protest was sparked by an event hosted by the 'SME-Union Middle Franconia' ('Mittelstands-Union Mittelfranken (MU)), which had invited lawyer Ulrich Vosgerau, known for defending persons like AfD member Bjorn Hocke. The 'Action Courage Erlangen' alliance ('Aktion Courage Erlangen') organized the demonstration, evaluating the MU as connected to far-right ideologies. Erlangen's Mayor, Florian Janik (SPD), also spoke at the event, emphasizing the need to stand against the spread of far-right views across the 'mainstream'.
On 1 September 2021, several thousand activists gathered for a rally in Kosice, protesting against the current government and coronavirus-related restrictions.
On 29 October 2021, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Karlstad to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.

On 20 October 2025, workers from public enterprises 'Parks and Greenery', 'Florakom', and 'Luna' protested in Skopje over unpaid September wages. Organized by the Independent Union of State Administration, the workers blocked a major intersection and warned of a full strike beginning October 28 if their demands are not met.

On 29 June 2023, overnight, rioters clashed with state forces (assumed police) in Chalon-sur-Saone (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte). The event was part of a national wave of riots and demonstrations denouncing police violence and demanding justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre on 27 June 2023.

On 7 February 2024, at the call of the National Group of Farmers and Ranchers of the Primary Sector (Agrupacion Nacional de Agricultores y Ganaderos del Sector Primario), around 600 farmers and a hundred tractors participated in a demonstration in Santa Fe and Vegas del Genil in Granada (Andalucia), clashing with the Civil Guard, who arrested 6 demonstrators. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and of the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector.

On 26 January 2021, around 300 teachers and education assistants demonstrated in Perpignan at the call of unions. They denounced their working conditions and the management of the coronavirus crisis by the government. They also called for a salary raise.

On 1 May 2023, 450 people took to the streets of Groix to demonstrate, expressing solidarity with Ukraine and demanding gender equality at work. The event was part of a 13th national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called on International Workers' Day by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to oppose the pension reform of the government, and call for its withdrawal.

On 30 June 2023, about 300 people, including a few doctors, gathered in Nocera Inferiore (Salerno, Campania) to protest against the envisaged transfer of 39 patients with disabilities from the hospital to a rest home that, according to the demonstrators, will not guarantee the right to treatment of their loved ones. The mayor, the vice-mayor and a councilor (all civic lists) of Roccapiemonte as well as a councilor of Pagani, and the provincial representatives of UIL and CISL took part in the demonstration.

On 25 November 2025, a handful of teachers protested at the Heilig Hart Institute in Heverlee in Leuven (Vlaanderen) against the government plants to increase teachers' retirement age and reduce retirement benefits. Teachers and assistants of the university KU Leuven picketed at the De Valk college too. The event was part of a special strike day for education, within a three-day nationwide strike across the public and private sectors called by ABVV-FGTB, ACV-CSC and ACLVB-CGSLB to protest against the Federal Government's reform plans.
On 9 July 2022, about 1000 LGBT activists gathered for a pride march in Kielce, demanding equal rights for people of all genders.
On 8 November 2021, hairdressers protested in Malaga (Andalucia), calling on the government to reduce the VAT rate (from 21% to 10%) applied to their labour sector.

On 5 June 2021, over 100 citizens called by the Platform in defense of the Train protested in Valle de Carranza (Bizkaia) railway station demanding to resume the train services suspended due to the outbreak of the coronavirus pandemic.

On 18 September 2025, in the afternoon, hundreds of people gathered at the theater in Brive-la-Gaillarde (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to demonstrate. Demonstrators subsequently marched through the city center to denounce government austerity policies, expressing grievances over inflation and healthcare access. The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration day called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, FSU, and SUD to oppose the government's draft 2026 budget, condemn austerity measures affecting public services and welfare, and denounce the perceived erosion of wages and social protections.
On 15 March 2023, SOR supporters and members protested in Nisporeni, demanding the resignation of the president and demanding that the government pay the winter utility bills.

On 14 November 2022, around 150 emergency personnel from the Hospital de la Ribera held a protest in Alcira (Valencia) against the management of the hospital and to demand improvements in their working conditions.

On 6 April 2024, at the call of the Dole Migrant Aid Collective (Collectif d'Aide aux Migrants de Dole), people gathered in Dole (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte) to protest against the passing of the new immigration law, which they deemed xenophobic and unfair to immigrants. They also condemned the harsh living conditions of refugees in France.

On 14 June 2025, at the call of Pink Festival, hundreds of LGBTQ+ community members and their supporters marched through the city center in Cambridge (England) as part of the city's annual pride event to celebrate and recognize the LGBTQ+ community and their contributions.

On 20 October 2020, health workers gathered in Sevilla to protest about excessive work overload during the coronavirus pandemic. Protesters demanded more human and material resources be allocated to the public health services. The demonstration was called by the Public Official's Independent Trade Union (CSIF), Workers Commissions (CCOO) and General Union of Workers (UGT).
On 3 May 2022, several journalists protested outside the Russian embassy in Chisinau - Buiucani, condemning the Russian attacks against the killed journalists in Ukraine.

On 19 March 2021, FFF activists gathered in the street in Vigevano (Pavia, Lombardia) to urge authorities to step up their efforts in the fight against the climate crisis. The event was part of the Global Climate Strike called internationally by FFF on that day.

On 4 June 2020, about 50 members of anti-establishment groups rallied in central Thessaloniki and marched to the United States Consulate to express their solidarity with the Black Lives Matter demonstrations in the United States over the death of George Floyd in police custody.

On 15 June 2020, about 1500 people took part in a Black Lives Matter march at Lemon Quay in Truro. They were met by a counter-demonstration of about 60 demonstrators who claimed to be there to protect the city's war memorial on Boscawen Street. About 200 of the Black Lives Matter demonstrators then confronted the people at the memorial, resulting in a stand-off in which the opposing sides threw things at each other. Police intervened and created a barrier between the two groups. Three Black Lives Matter campaigners were arrested, and one counter-demonstrator was arrested for a racially aggravated public order offence.

On 14 February 2024, a group of activists protested during a parliamentary session in Stockholm to call for an end to arms sales to Israel and to oppose the ongoing Israeli offensive in Gaza and Rafah. The activists were later removed by police, seven people were arrested.

On 19 July 2025, citizens and students cycled from Novi Sad and arrived in Sirig, protesting against the ruling regime, demanding extraordinary parliamentary elections, and condemning the police brutality towards peacefully protesting students.

On 13 August 2021, about 100 people, including relatives of the victim, took to the streets in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to demonstrate against police brutality. The event was organized by the parents of German national Sammy Baker, who was shot dead by police upon his arrest in Nieuw-West the year prior.
On 22 February 2025, citizens gathered in Arandelovac, demanding accountability for the loss of 15 lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the Novi Sad railway station.
On 23 September 2022, at the call of FFF, people gathered for a protest in Bordeaux, to demand more action on the issue of climate change.

On 1 October 2024, several students protested at the National School of Political and Administrative Studies in Bucharest, demanding action against abuses in universities, particularly in light of allegations against sociologist Alfred Bulai. The protesters called for systemic reforms to create safer university environments and improve mechanisms for handling complaints. Bulai, currently under house arrest, is accused of sexual harassment and abuse of office.

On 21 November 2024, people gathered outside the district council in Grevesmuhlen (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern), to protest against the closure of a counseling center for victims of domestic violence. Organizers displayed nearly 160 pairs of shoes, each symbolizing a person who had been supported by the center over the past two years.

On 25 January 2024, about 250 activists gathered for a rally in Humenne, protesting against what they see as unacceptable meddling into democratic institutions and processes in Slovakia. The protests were triggered by the recent announcement of the ruling Smer party to abolish a special prosecutor's office, which is responsible for investigating high-profile corruption cases.

On 14 May 2026, 4 MPs from the Democracy at Home (DA) opposition faction held a peaceful protest outside the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Chisinau - Centru (Chisinau), timed to coincide with the Foreign Minister's meeting with his Norwegian counterpart who was in Chisinau for a Council of Europe Committee of Ministers session. Protesters displayed a banner demanding the release of a Moldovan-Ukrainian dual citizen and accused the authorities of failing to act to repatriate him after his reported detention at the Rososhany-Briceni border crossing for Ukrainian military mobilization, framing the war in Ukraine as not Moldova's concern.
On 12 July 2020, around 2,500 people protested in Dresden under the motto 'Black Lives Matter - No to Racism' against racism, discrimination and police violence.
On 20 October 2023, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Malmo, Skane, to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.

On 11 December 2025, around 100 members of the Animal welfare organisation Invisible Animals protested in front of Stenbock House in Tallinn, Estonia, in support of a bill to ban the keeping of chickens in cages. The protesters believe that the government is not quick enough with putting the bill on its agenda since its submission in October.

On 31 January 2025, medical staff from Smederevska Palanka gathered in front of General Hospital 'Stefan Visoki' to observe 15 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign, to honor the victims who lost their lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the Novi Sad train station and demand accountability for their deaths.

On 23 November 2024, hundreds of people including fishers, gathered under the Ognina Bridge in Catania (Sicilia) to protest against the privatization of Borgo Marinaro, following the concession issued by the Region to expand the tourist port which, according to protesters, would prevent citizens' access to one of the few sea views of the city. M5S, ARCI, EV, Legambiente, LIPU, the PD regional secretary, PRC, SI, WWF and local associations took part in the event's organization.

On 15 November 2023, several tens of employees of the pensions fund company, the employment agency, the social payments agency, as well as around 40 employees of the public health department, protested in Miercurea Ciuc, demanding higher salaries.

On 1 October 2024, around 1,000 people demonstrated in Le Mans (Pays de la Loire). The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration day called by CGT, SUD, and FSU to demand better public service, protest against state budget cuts, and defend workers' rights. The protesters also criticized what they saw as an undemocratic rightward shift in the government, arguing that President Emmanuel Macron ignored the strong performance of the left in the legislative elections by appointing Michel Barnier (LR) as Prime Minister.

On 25 November 2024, on the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, around 350 people including students and members of feminist associations marched from Sant'Anna park to Del Bacio Square in Perugia (Umbria) to protest against gender violence.

On 15 July 2025, citizens blocked the central roundabout in Cacak, protesting against the ruling regime, demanding extraordinary parliamentary elections, and condemning the police brutality towards peacefully protesting students.

On 5 March 2022, around 40 persons demonstrated on the market of Chasseneuil at the call of a feminist organization. They gathered on the occasion of the upcoming International women's rights day to denounce violence against women and call for equal labor rights and salaries between men and women.

On 29 June 2021, over 400 environmental activists, including XR members, occupied four sites, three of the company Lafarge, in Gennevilliers (Nanterre, Hauts-de-Seine, Ile-de-France) to protest against the company, urbanization, and the ruining of the landscape with concrete buildings. Protesters stayed there overnight.

On 25 July 2023, around 100 anti-racism activists gathered outside the police station in London - Croydon (England) following the release of video footage of the wrongful arrest of a Black mother for bus fare evasion a few days earlier. Campaigners raised concerns over police treatment of Black communities. The protest was organized by SUTR, BLM Croydon, Disabled People Against Cuts (DPAC), and RMT Black & Ethnic Minority Members.

On 18 December 2025, at the call of CP, around 175 farmers gathered in Saint-Lo (Normandie). The event was part of a nationwide demonstration movement by farmers against the mass culling of cattle herds in cases of lumpy skin disease, following the contested euthanasia of 207 cows on a farm in Bordes-sur-Arize. Participants demanded alternative measures, such as the killing of animals affected by the disease only, and mass vaccinations. More broadly, farmers opposed the Mercosur-EU trade agreement, arguing that increased meat imports would drive prices down and further threaten already precarious farm incomes.
On 11 August 2018, protesters in Targu Mures rallied against corruption and the policies of the Romanian government.

On 25 February 2026, at 11:30 am, at the call of PAH and Together for Housing (Junts per l'Habitatge), people protested outside the Department of Housing in Valencia (Valencia) to demand solutions to tackle the city's housing crisis, calling for an increase in rental aid funding and an end to eviction of vulnerable families.

On 26 August 2022, at the call of a regional councilor (Mixed group), people rallied in front of the prefecture in Foggia (Foggia, Puglia) to demand that the allocated budget for the highway 16 be used to increase safety and quality of the concerned infrastructure. They also demanded the adoption of counter measures to tackle drought affecting the region's agricultural sector.

On 29 October 2024, at the call of CGT, SUD, UNSA, and FO, around 10 striking health workers gathered for a picket line outside the hospital in Roubaix (Hauts-de-France) to demand increased state funding for public healthcare amid the recent approval of the new social security budget, voicing concerns about budget cuts, inadequate staffing, and worsening work conditions, and highlighting the recent increase in burnout and long-term illness among healthcare staff.

On 6 September 2023, Last Generation activists protested with a sit-in in front of the train station in Stuttgart (Baden-Wurttemberg) to show solidarity with fellow activists in Munich, especially those taken into preventive custody until the end of the International Mobility Show Germany (IAA Mobility) taking place in the city. Moreover, 12 Last Generation activists protested on Arnulf-Klett-Platz with a slow protest march, against the climate policies of the government and the imprisonment of other activists. The police intervened in both cases, carrying the activists off the road.

On 1 February 2024, farmers blocked access to a logistical platform in Avallon (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte). The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement called by FNSEA and JA against rising production costs, stricter environmental norms restricting the use of pesticides, foreign imports, and bureaucratic constraints.
On 23 February 2020, several hundred people held a vigil in Remscheid for the victims of the Hanau attack and to take a stand against racism and for tolerance and democracy.

On 22 November 2023, at the call of Non Una di Meno, about 6,000 people and women took to the streets in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to commemorate Giulia Cecchettin, 22 year-old killed by her ex-boyfriend, and all victims of femicide and protest against violence against women.

On 30 November 2024, people marched in Ostersund, Jamtland, to protest against racism and xenophobia. The activists also expressed their strong dissatisfaction with the government's proposal to oblige public sector employees to report irregular immigrants and undocumented people.

On 6 December 2023, protesters gathered in Vidin to demand a bigger budget for cultural institutions that would ensure stability and fair wages. Protests were held in several locations in Bulgaria, with both cultural workers and their supporters taking place.
On 12 December 2020, around 200 persons gathered at the Bellecour square in Lyon. They demonstrated against islamophobia and racism, at the call of the SUD union for students.
On 8 April 2022, Fridays for Future activists demonstrated in Malmo to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.
On 9 December 2022, Fridays for Future activists demonstrated in front of the city hall in Malmo to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.

On 28 July 2024, more than 100 people gathered outside Taymouth Castle Estate in Aberfeldy (Scotland) to highlight the impact of the concentration of ownership of Scottish land in a few hands. On 24 February 2024, at the call of the Italian Network for Peace and Disarmament, a large group of people took to the streets of Avellino (Campania) to protest against all wars and demand the end of the Russia-Ukraine and Israeli-Palestinian conflicts.

On 1 August 2025, fishermen gathered for a rally in Nove Mlyny, protesting against what they see as extensive environmental damage caused by a local water energy power plant.

On 30 June 2023, overnight, demonstrators took to the streets of the Haut-Champs neighborhood of Hem to riot.
