On 29 August 2025, citizens blocked the road near Fontana in Belgrade - Novi Beograd, to protest against the ruling regime and police brutality during the recent protests.

On 6 March 2025, around 100 people, including health workers and the mayor (UDR), gathered in front of the hospital in Mamers (Sarthe) to protest against the changes to summer leave planning, arguing it would reduce the number of staff allowed to take time off simultaneously.

On 20 September 2020, around 600 people staged a protest on the Jaarbeursplein in Utrecht to denounce the situation of the refugees in the Greek refugee camp Moria on Lesbos, which was destroyed by a fire in the previous week.
On 20 December 2024, workers from CNE union protested at the Aldi distribution center in Gembloux (Wallonie), over unresolved labor issues after more than two years of negotiations.

On 14 March 2025, around 500 members of the local Moto Club drove at a slow pace to protest through the city center before gathering outside the motorbike track in Bordeaux (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to demand the eviction of members of the Traveler community who had been living on the track since 20 December 2024.
On 24 February 2023, people and members of the Ukrainian community held a protest in Leiria (Leiria) on the year anniversary of Russia's invasion of Ukraine to demand the end of the war.

On 27 March 2024, hundreds of students, teachers, and parents protested in front of the office of the Minister for Education of the Dutch-speaking community in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) against the teacher shortage in the capital.

On 10 May 2024, about 200 people, among which some students of the University of Amsterdam (UvA), protested in front of the Stopera in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) during an emergency debate at the City Council's General Affairs Committee on the pro-Palestinian demonstrations of the past days at the University of Amsterdam. The protesters demanded that the UvA be transparent about collaborations with Israeli institutions and companies and cut all ties with Israeli institutions.

On 8 June 2024, LGBTQ+ activists gathered for a pride march through Warsaw, demanding equal rights for people of all genders. A minor group of counter-protesters gathered nearby, but no skirmishes were reported.

Around 18 June 2020, an unknown number of health workers staged a protest in Deerlijk in the context of a national action day against the underfunding of the health sector. The action was organized by ACV Puls.

On 3 June 2020, around 500 people gathered at Guildhall Square in Southampton for a Black Lives Matter protest, demonstrating against police brutality after the killing of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.

On 8 March 2026, at the call of Non Una di Meno, hundreds of people, including students, gathered in Perugia (Umbria) to protest patriarchy, sexism, and violence against women, and to demand gender equality in every aspect of life, from equal pay to women's rights and bodily autonomy. They also demonstrated against a law proposal they considered lacking and ineffective, namely the DDL Bongiorno, which aims to regulate issues related to sexual violence and consent. Protesters condemned the US-Israeli attack against Iran. The event was held as part of a nationwide demonstration on International Women's Day.

On 28 May 2021, around 30 protesters led by Black Lives Matter activists marched through Newport city center to mark 100 days since the death of a black man who died approximately two hours after police attended a property on 17 February. Protesters called on police to release bodycam footage and demanded justice for the man.

On 6 October 2020, several hundred people, including workers of nursing homes, protested in San Sebastian (Gipuzkoa) demanding better working conditions and a dignified collective labor agreement. Protesters complained about extreme tiredness and exhaustion due to work overload during the coronavirus pandemic. The demonstration was called by the Abertzales Workers' Committees (LAB) and Basque Workers' Association (ELA).
On 18 January 2024, around 40 family doctors and medical assistants protested in Botosani, condemning the small allocations for family medicine.

On 20 February 2024, farmers blocked roads around Kalisz, protesting against ongoing imports of grains from Ukraine and also against what they see as an excessive bureaucracy related to the so-called Green Deal of the European Union.

On 19 November 2025, over 200 former employees of the furniture company 'Krivaja' protested in front of the Government of the Federation in Sarajevo, demanding the payment of their unpaid salaries, for those who have met the conditions for retirement to be granted their pensions, as well as a transparent sale of the company's property.

On 22 April 2024, at the call of the 'Let's Save Pellerina Committee' (Comitato Salviamo Pellerina), the 'Future Generation Cooperative' (Generazioni Future Cooperative), and the 'Piedmont Coordination for Human Rights' (Cordinamento per i Diritti Umani Piemonte), people, including environmental activists, gathered outside the town hall in Torino (Piemonte) to demand more climate action and denounce the responsibility of the mayor and all members of the city council in a lack of related policies. Demonstrators protested against the administration's greenwashing, the cutting of trees in public parks and gardens, and the lack of attention given to the Pellerina Hospital.

On 17 August 2024, thousands of LGBTQ+ community members and their supporters marched through Colchester (England) as part of the city's annual pride event to celebrate the LGBTQIA+ community and call for the protection of its members' rights.
On 26 June 2021, citizens, including LGBT activists, staged a pride parade in Logrono. They claimed the right of each individual to express their gender identity.
On 25 September 2020, around 1,000 Fridays for Future activists protested in Mainz for more climate action as part of a Global Climate Strike.

On 3 November 2022, in the evening, at the call of the collective 'La Super Cour des Miracles', around 50 activists gathered in rue de Damiette in Paris to demonstrate against the eviction by private security forces of a vacant apartment previously occupied by the collective to help homeless migrants and host artistic initiatives.

On 18 May 2026, environmental activists demonstrated outside Stockholm District Court in Stockholm to show support and solidarity with a climate activist involved in a lawsuit against the Swedish state over claims that she was fired due to her activism. Activists from an Extinction Rebellion associated group, Extinction Rebellion and Greenpeace participated in the event, among others.

On 27 November 2021, climate activists, including The Greens and Extinction Rebellion members, occupying Lobau Camp protested in Vienna - Donaustadt against the construction of the Lobau tunnel and called on authorities to do more to tackle climate change.
On 8 June 2019, parents organized a protest in Blagoevgrad against the National Strategy for the Child.

On 9 March 2024, people, including an LFI MP, the mayors of Brionne (PCF) and Serquigny (unspecified affiliation), and other elected representatives, gathered in Bernay (Normandie) to defend public services.

On 19 August 2023, around 700 people participated in the Christopher Street Day (CSD) in Neubrandenburg (Mecklenburgische Seenplatte, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern) to protest for acceptance, tolerance and self-determination of LGBTQ+.

On 12 January 2021, around 50 unionized health workers and social workers protested in Alba Iulia, complaining over the delayed raise of the minimum wage and the poor protection equipment in the fight against the coronavirus.
On 20 January 2020, about 1,500 Pegida supporters took part in a protest march in Dresden. About 100 counterprotesters, demonstrating against hate and racism, took to the street.
On 26 May 2024, dozens of residents held a protest in O Carballino (Ourense, Galicia) to demand the recruitment of pediatricians at the municipality's health center.
On 16 February 2023, hundreds of students staged a protest march in Mons against the Wallonie-Bruxelles government's decision to not provide a master's program in medicine at the University of Mons.

On 2 December 2023, representatives of Slovakian labor unions of truck drivers continued their blockade of the border crossing point with Ukraine in Vysne Nemecke, declaring solidarity with their Polish counterparts. The Polish activists have been blocking the Poland-Ukraine border for several days, criticizing allegedly unfair economic competition.

On 8 June 2024, more than 1,000 people, called by Via Menorca, held a protest in Menorca (coded to Mahon) (Islas Baleares) against the current model of mass tourism, claiming it pushed residents away.

On 19 July 2025, activists organized by the Confederation party and football fan groups gathered for numerous rallies and marches across Poland, including in Krakow, protesting against increased immigration to the country. A counter-rally organized by the Coalition Against Racism was held nearby, praising solidarity instead. The marches were preceded by several cases of violence between immigrants of various backgrounds and the local population, as well as by an increased migration flow across the German and Belarusian borders.

On 23 February 2020, tens of people, including Unirea Movement, USB and PL members, marched from the Moldovan presidency building to the Russian embassy in Chisinau, demanding the resignation of president Dodon and the withdrawal of the Russian troops.
On 6 December 2022, Animal Save movement activists held a vigil in front of a meat processing facility in Kristianstad, Skane, to oppose animal rights violations and to promote animal welfare.

On 21 December 2022, Turkish-Cypriot school janitors, organized by Kamu-Is, marched to the Presidency in Northern Nicosia for their rights and they demanded a collective labor agreement. They also protested for the second day that janitors in public schools were dismissed because they were union members.
On 12 May 2023, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Lund, Skane, to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.
On 13 January 2020, farmers gathered in Bielsk Podlaski, demanding economic guarantees in a process of bankruptcy of a local large company.

On 8 January 2022, protesters organized by the Ecological Uprising gathered in Preljina as part of environmental protests against the planned construction of the Rio Tinto lithium mine in the country.

On 28 March 2022, around 80 people staged a protest action in Lo-Reninge, forming a silent circle to denounce the Russian invasion of Ukraine.
On 20 June 2023, hundreds of youth workers protested in Liege (Wallonie), to demand better working conditions in their sector, more staff, and better infrastructure.

On 7 August 2023, people demonstrated outside of a stud farm in Skals, Viborg, accusing the farm owner of animal cruelty and severe animal rights violations. Police personnel were present to ensure the security of the event.
On 20 February 2020, about 300 BIW workers protested in Ennepetal against feared job cuts.

On 15 December 2022, care and community health assistants (ASSC) workers gathered for a picket in front of the Carouge offices of IMAD in Geneva, to demand better working conditions.

The residents opposed the municipal council's decision to allocate nearly 40 acres of land for the project, citing environmental risks, lack of public consultation, and insufficient technical assessments.

On 2 July 2020, nurses gathered in Lisbon to demand solutions to the problems that their sector is suffering, such as the 'discrimination' in the current career system. Protesters also demanded better salary conditions.

On 27 September 2021, local residents protested in Bor, Serbia, against pollution coming from the near-by copper-mining company.

On 8 March 2024, hundreds of people demonstrated in Stavanger, Rogaland, to mark the International Women's Day and in support of women's rights.

On 25 October 2024, at the call of CR, around 40 farmers gathered outside the Prefecture, staged a mock funeral, and dumped tires in Perigueux (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to demand more financial state support for farmers.

On 3 June 2020, up to 70 people gathered in front of Town Hall in Stratford-upon-Avon for a Black Lives Matter protest organized by Stand Up To Racism, demonstrating against police brutality after the killing of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.

On 22 February 2024, several hundred Czech and Polish farmers blocked a border crossing point near Paczkow, protesting against the ongoing imports of grains from Ukraine and also against what they see as an excessive bureaucracy related to the so-called Green Deal of the European Union.
On 20 November 2020, seven Fridays For Future activists staged a protest in Jonkoping to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.
On 13 January 2020, about 40 farmers protested in Baunatal against the tightening of the environmental regulations.
On 25 August 2023, Animal Save activists demonstrated in Stockholm to oppose animal rights violations and to promote animal welfare and plant-based diets.
On 18 January 2023, teachers and technicians protested in Seixal (Setubal) to demand improvements in the working conditions of education professionals.

On 10 September 2025, around 20 people staged a roadblock in Martigues (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to demonstrate. The event was part of the 'Let's Block Everything' (Bloquons Tout) strike and demonstration movement against the French government's planned fiscal austerity measures, the lack of adequate democratic representation, and inequality.

On 6 November 2020, cultural workers protested in Ljubljana against the plan to open a museum dedicated to Slovenia's independence, claiming it would further decrease the already scarce funds allocated to the cultural sector.

On 6 December 2022, at least 40 people, mainly migrants, blocked the street next to Porte de la Chapelle in Paris, to demand the regularization of their status. Police officers, making use of tear gas, removed them from the spot.
On 15 September 2022, farmers gathered for a protest ride around Litomysl, demanding higher support for the Czech agriculture.

On 5 February 2023, people, summoned by the No a la Caza platform, held a protest in Almeria (Andalucia) to demand the inclusion of hunting and working dogs in the Animal Welfare Law, which is set to be debated and voted on in the Congress of Deputies on 9 February 2023.

On 1 May 2021, nearly 7,000 persons, including members of the NPA, health workers and teachers demonstrated in Bordeaux at the call of the CGT union on the occasion of Labour Day. They called for social justice and denounced police violence.
On 31 July 2022, more than 200 people gathered for a Pride March from rue de la Republique to Place du Palais-des-Papes in Avignon, in support of LGBT rights.

On 14 April 2026, at the call of several entities such as CGT, dozens of people protested outside the regional Parliament in Valladolid (Castilla y Leon) against planned biogas plant projects in rural areas, criticizing the development of such projects in depopulated rural areas for the sake of renewable energies. Protesters cited environmental concerns.
On 14 December 2021, midwives gathered in front of the Beauregard private hospital in Marseille at the call of the CGT union. They called for more staff and a salary raise.
On 12 May 2018, a protest was held in Craiova against the policies conducted by the Social-Democratic government.

On 17 September 2024, at the call of UGVC - General Union of Cognac Winegrowers (Union Generale des Viticulteurs pour l'AOC Cognac), between 800 and 1,000 farmers, winegrowers, and salespeople, drove 120 tractors at a slow pace to protest from several localities in the area and gathered outside the Sub-Prefecture in Cognac (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against Chinese authorities' decision to impose import taxes on French Cognac, threatening the revenues of the Cognac industry. The protesters urged the European Union (EU) to financially support them and advocated for a cancellation of the Chinese taxes.
On 17 September 2020, around 100 health workers protested outside a hospital in Focsani, demanding the payment of the promised benefits and vacation vouchers.
On 7 December 2025, people protested in Muro (Islas Baleares) against bullfighting.

On 1 October 2025, students and citizens gathered in Nis to mark the 11 months since the concrete canopy collapsed at the Novi Sad railway station, resulting in the deaths of 16 people. The protest concluded with a 16-minute silence to honor the victims and to demand justice and accountability for their deaths.

On 21 January 2023, around 20 people protested in front of the Russian Embassy in Riga, Lavia calling against the political repression in Russia and demanding to free Russian opposition politician Alexei Navalny and other political prisoners.

On 25 March 2025, a few hundred employees from the University of Twente, including professors, participated in a protest against cuts to higher education, starting on the university campus and moving toward the city center of Enschede (Overijssel). The protest was part of a nationwide strike against the government's planned 1.2 billion euro cuts to higher education.

On 25 January 2026, 6,500 to 8,000 people, among them union members, including ACV-CSC, representatives of the political parties Ecolo, PS and PTB, and families with children, gathered in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest against the planned budget cuts in French higher education by the education minister Valerie Glatigny (MR). Protesters feared the plans would destroy the chances of Belgian children in the future.
On 27 June 2025, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Lund, Skane, to draw attention to environmental issues and to demand action against climate change.

On 1 March 2024, Turkish Cypriot protesters organized by the Environment Platform rallied outside the Ministry of Agriculture in Northern Nicosia to protest over the risks that beetle insects were posing to forests. The head of Greenpeace in Northern Cyprus, political parties and NGOs participated in the protest.

On 26 December 2024, animal rights activists protested in front of the Parliament in Chisinau - Buiucani, against a proposed law on animal protection. The protesters claimed that the new law only applies to companion animals and lacks provisions for public oversight, a dolphinarium ban, mandatory video recording for animal capture, and government support for shelters and volunteers.
On 22 November 2020, around 25 people staged a protest in Kortrijk to denounce violence against women in the context of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

On 1 September 2025, at around 7 pm, at the call of an activist from The Homeland, between 50 and 100 people, including supporters from Hildburghausen, gathered in Leinefelde (Thuringen) for a mourning march combined with the regular Monday demonstration in memory of a 16-year-old Ukrainian girl who died after being pushed onto train tracks. Participants used the event to protest against violence by migrants with unresolved asylum status and criticized the government's migration policy. At the same time, counter-demonstrators, including left-wing activists from Gottingen and the Eichsfeld, rallied nearby to oppose what they described as xenophobic and nationalist messaging. The march proceeded under heavy police presence, and confrontations between the groups remained verbal.

On 20 May 2024, about 30 pro-Palestine protesters from the North Wicklow Against Genocide group held a protest outside the prime minister's constituency office in Bray (Wicklow) to call on the government to stop blocking the Occupied Territories Bill. The Bill would ban any goods or services produced in the Israeli-occupied territories from being traded in Ireland.
On 7 April 2023, farmers drove their tractors and vehicles at the border crossing point in Nadlac in protest to the dumping prices of tariff-free Ukrainian products.

On 21 May 2021, a dozen students demonstrated in Nijmegen (Gelderland) to protest against the current student loan system. Protesters demanded the system's abolition and compensation for those students who were taken advantage of by that system.
On 19 July 2023, Animal Save Movement activists demonstrated in various locations of Boras, Vastra Gotaland, to oppose zoos, animal rights violations and to promote plant-based diet.

On 20 June 2023, around 100 health workers of a nearby clinic gathered in Mosbach (Baden-Wurttemberg), to protest against a planned reform for clinics in Germany. The protest was part of a national protest day for the financial situation of clinics.

On 9 March 2023, around 110 people gathered at Theodor-Heuss-Platz in Hannover to protest against a show by historian Daniele Ganser. The mayor Belit Onay of The Greens, addressed the protesters and called on them to resist conspiracy theories and antisemitism. A counter-protest with around 65 people was organised by BPD to support Ganser.

On 15 June 2024, between 7,000 and 8,000 people demonstrated in Rodez (Occitanie). The event was part of a nationwide wave of demonstrations against racism, far-right ideology, and in support of an open society called by CGT, CFDT, FSU, UNSA, and SUD. The event took place after the National Rally (RN) came first in the European elections in France and President Emmanuel Macron announced the dissolution of the National Assembly on 9 June, raising fears of a government led by the far-right party. The demonstrators demanded all parties from the left to unite in a 'Popular Front' (Front Populaire) ahead of the upcoming legislative elections.

On 10 June 2025, demonstrators took to the streets for an anti-migration protest in Belfast - West (Northern Ireland) and blocked the Carlisle Circus roundabout, causing traffic destruction. Around 50 demonstrators also blocked Shankill Road and held placards that read 'protect our children'. The event was part of a wave of anti-migration demonstrations that erupted across Northern Ireland, following the charging of two Romanian-speaking teenagers with attempted rape in connection to the alleged sexual assault of a teenage girl in Ballymena.

On 21 August 2023, feminist activists and civil society representatives protested against femicide in Rijeka. The protesters paid tribute to the femicide victim in Gradacac, Bosnia and Herzegovina, who her husband viciously murdered.

On 27 June 2023, rioters took to the streets, vandalizing and setting fire to street furniture, in Saint-Denis (Ile-de-France). Police shot rubber bullets (LBD) at the rioters to fend them off. The event was part of a national wave of riots and demonstrations denouncing police violence and demanding justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre on 27 June 2023.
On 21 May 2022, hundreds of RFSU activists demonstrated in Stockholm to draw attention to the issue of infant mortality and in support of reproductive rights.

On 17 July 2025, county-pension-house employees affiliated with National Union Bloc- Blocul National Sindical (BNS) staged a peaceful protest outside the County Pension House in Piatra Neamt (Piatra-Neamt, Neamt), denouncing the Government's austerity package that caps 'hazard' allowances, cuts extra leave and perpetuates pay inequities. Action was part of a BNS-coordinated national series of demonstrations at county pension offices.
On 1 October 2020, about 200 students of the Warsaw University gathered for a rally, protesting against the president's anti-LGBT claims.

On 16 January 2022, about 1000 activists gathered for a rally in Pardubice, protesting against coronavirus-related measures, including vaccination. Among them, representatives of various labor unions and professions were present.

They condemned the proposed law as it could reinforce discrimination and inequality in working-class neighborhoods according to them.
On 31 May 2020, a Black Lives Matter protest, organized by the Samidoun network, gathered in Brunnsparken in Goteborg. The protest addressed racism and political violence in Sweden.

On 23 March 2024, at the call of Anti-Racist Platform of Navarra (Plataforma Antirracista de Navarra), people protested in Pamplona (Navarra) to demand a commitment to combat structural, social and institutional racism.

During the protest march, activists peacefully occupied some rooms of the City Council in Verdi Street. Some activists tried to occupy UniCredit bank but they were stopped by the police, without the use of force.

On 30 June 2023, overnight, rioters vandalized and damaged street furniture and buildings in Annemasse (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes). Police officers used tear gas to disperse the rioters. The event was part of a national wave of riots and demonstrations denouncing police violence and demanding justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre on 27 June 2023.

On 6 February 2024, teachers, including SNES-FSU affiliates, gathered for a picket line outside the Carco school in Villefranche-de-Rouergue (Occitanie) to demand higher wages and better working conditions in public schools after Minister of Education Amelie Oudea-Castera issued comments they deemed disrespectful to teachers. They also protested against plans to sort students into different level groups.

On 27 January 2024, people took part in a protest in Gera (Thuringen) against right-wing extremism. The protest was prompted by concerns over a secret meeting between AfD representatives and other far-right activists, discussing mass deportations of individuals with German citizenship and migrant background, leading to a heightened awareness and mobilization against far-right ideas in various cities.

On 4 July 2025, at the call of UPA and COAG, around 200 people, including Portuguese and Spanish nationals, blocked the A52 road near Padornelo (Viana do Castelo) to demand the reinstatement of train stop frequencies in Otero and A Gudina. Protesters denounced the suppression of morning services as detrimental to rural mobility, medical access, and tourism, and called for equitable transport provision for the region.

On 25 February 2024, at the call of FFF, around 4,000 people staged a protest in Bregenz (Vorarlberg) against right-wing extremism and in support of human rights and democracy. They gathered in solidarity with similar protests across Germany and Austria, linking the defense of democracy with the need to address the impact of climate change on human rights and global migration.

On 20 August 2022, an unknown number of activists of TFP Student Action Europe staged a protest in front of the Sint-Niklaas church in Gent to denounce abortion as murder. At the same time, around 50 LGBT activists assembled as a counterprotest on the same location.

On 3 November 2021, nurses demonstrated in front of Roskilde Hospital in Roskilde to demand an increase in wages for healthcare workers and to show dissatisfaction with the outcome of the nurses' strike. The demonstration was a part of the nationwide protest action held across the country on 3 November 2021.

On 24 January 2025, protesters gathered in front of the municipality of Tirana demanding the resignation of the mayor and the government led by the ruling Socialist Party. They also demand that what they claim are witch-hunts against the Democratic Party be suspended, claiming that the recent spate of arrests and trials are a political move orchestrated by the ruling party to diminish the Democratic Party's influence in the country.
On 8 March 2021, citizens staged a caravan protest in Merida demanding gender equality on International Women's Day.
On 26 April 2023, between 4 and 8 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic at the border crossing Au (Switzerland) and Lustenau on the Austrian side to call for climate protection.

On 14 February 2026, people demonstrated in Kristiansand, Agder, to protest the occupation and what they described as Israel's genocide in Gaza. Among other things, the activists called for a boycott of Israel and for the Norwegian Oil Fund to divest from companies linked to Israel. The event was organized by the Norway's Palestine Committee.

On 27 May 2023, hundreds of members of Just Stop Oil, Extinction Rebellion, Black Lives Matter, and Republican activists gathered in Parliament Square in London - Westminster against Government's Public Order Bill limiting the right to protest. Protests carried 'No more police powers' and 'Defend the right to protest' banners.
On 25 November 2022, women demonstrated in Varnamo, Jonkoping on the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women and in support of women's rights.

On 24 January 2024, in the morning, a large crowd rallied outside the home of a retired journalist in Zografou, Athens - Central Athens, to protest her eviction after she lost her primary home in a foreclosure and the new owner filed a lawsuit against her. Police broke down the door and arrested her. MAT riot police used tear gas on the crowd, following verbal confrontations. The solidarity protesters then gathered outside Zografou police station shouting 'No home in the hands of a banker'. Police used tear gas and pushed the crowd that had formed a cordon out of the way, as they were transporting the retired journalist to the Evelpidon court. The Association of Photojournalists of Greece reported that police hit on the head a photo reporter covering the event at the police station. The crowd then moved to the court complex shouting slogans of encouragement as the retired journalist was released after a trial date was set, while labor unions organized a rally that attracted hundreds outside her home in the evening.

On 30 June 2021, environmental hygiene workers gathered, at the call of FP CGIL, FIT CISL, UILTrasporti (UIL) and FIADEL, outside the Prefecture in Lecce (Lecce, Puglia) to call for a revamp of Article 177 of the new Procurement Code, which would allegedly prompt companies from the sector to externalize their services and dismiss workers following the expiry of application extensions at the end of the year. The event was part of a national day of protest called by trade union branches active within the sector.

On 28 July 2022, around 30 people, including members of Out and Proud, gathered for a protest outside Aston Hall in Birmingham during the Queen's baton relay ahead of the Commonwealth Games opening ceremony against homophobia in the Commonwealth.
On 11 December 2021, activists affiliated with Feminist Revolutionary Brigade gathered for a rally in Torun, demanding higher solidarity with refugees stranded at the border with Belarus.

On 26 January 2022, protesters affiliated with the Social Democratic Party of Kosovo gathered in front of the government building in Pristina to demand that the electricity prices in the country be lowered. The prices have gone up several times since the end of last year since the Kosovo government declared a state of emergency.

On 11 November 2023, several hundred people gathered in Ajaccio (Corse) to demand a ceasefire in Gaza, show support for the Palestinian people, and condemn the Israeli military campaign in and around Gaza.
On 27 October 2022, students and teachers protested in Dunakeszi, demanding better pay for teachers, more teaching staff, and more academic freedom.

On 21 September 2024, protesters participated in a mass rally and march in Athens - Central Athens to mark the 6th anniversary since the killing of LGBTQ+ activist Zak Kostopoulos, shouting antifascist slogans. They were observed by strong police forces. They also demanded the street, where the murder took place, be renamed in honor of the activist.

On 16 December 2020, people working in the cultural sector gathered in Castello Square in Milano - Municipio 1 to demand from the government a better plan for facing the economic crisis created by the coronavirus pandemic. Knowledge Network supported the demonstration.
On 16 November 2023, around 500 people, summoned by Coordinadora por la Vivienda Digna, held a protest in Andorra la Vella (Andorrra) to demand dignified housing.

On 18 October 2023, protesters marched in solidarity with the Palestinian people in the region of Elis (coded to Pyrgos). Labor groups, civil society organizations, student associations, members of the extra-parliamentary left and of anti-establishment groups participated in the demonstration.
On 17 October 2020, animal rights activists from the Animal Alliance movement gathered in Aalborg to oppose fur industry and animal rights' violations at mink farms in Denmark.

On 24 March 2021, a dozen activists of Extinction Rebellion, WeMoveEurope and Birdlife Europe staged a protest at Schuman Square in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles to demand a revision of the EU Common Agricultural Policy.

On 21 September 2022, a family occupied a hospital room at the Four Pavillons clinic in Lormont, to denounce the clinic's management after one of their members had health complications following an operation.
On 15 March 2022, around 80 airport employees demonstrated in front of the airport in Hannover at the call of Ver.di union to call for better working conditions, more staff, and better pay.

On 11 February 2025, around 50 national police officers, as well as elected members of Vox and PP, called by the Unified Police Union (Sindicato Unido de Policia - SUP), held a protest outside the government delegation in Barcelona - Ciutat Vella (Cataluna) against transferring immigration powers to the Catalan government, as it would diminish their role.
On 13 July 2020, around 150 persons gathered in Sisteron. They protested for the reopening of the emergency room of the hospital at night.

On 23 March 2022, citizens protested in Huesca (Aragon), demanding that the government provide urgent measures to cope with the rising energy and fuel prices due to the coronavirus pandemic and the Russian invasion of Ukraine. The CCOO and UGT called the demonstration.

On 20 July 2020, about 2000 residents of Ostrava gathered for a rally, protesting against alleged lack of competence of the Minister of Health and demanding his resignation over recently-imposed measures related to the current coronavirus pandemic.

On 29 June 2023, about 20 people, including CGT affiliates, held a protest in front of the CEA center in Saint-Paul-les-Durance, on the occasion of the visit of the Minister of Research and Education, calling for better work conditions. Some denounced the government's pension reform.

On 6 July 2025, at the call of the ADFC, around 400 cyclists staged a protest ride from Heidelberg and Schwetzingen to Mannheim (Baden-Wurttemberg) to demand safer cycling infrastructure. The demonstration followed a deadly cycling accident in Mannheim the previous week and included a moment of silence in remembrance of the victim. Protesters highlighted the urgency of creating secure and continuous bike lanes to prevent further fatalities and improve road safety for cyclists.

On 11 January 2023, hundreds of people staged a demonstration in Ancona (Ancona, Marche) in support of the Ocean Viking humanitarian ship that was docking in the port of Ancona with migrants onboard. Demonstrators displayed a banner reading 'No to the criminalization of NGOs'. Amnesty International and self-managed social center activists took part in the demonstration.

On 11 August 2024, hundreds of LGBTQ+ community members and their supporters marched through Darlington (England) as part of the city's annual pride event, to celebrate the LGBTQIA+ community and defend its members' rights, as well as unity, acceptance, and love.

On 10 October 2025, at the call of FLC CGIL, striking teachers and school workers staged a picket outside the BAC - Music Park building in Taranto (Puglia) to protest the latest reform of the Italian Secondary Technical Schools (ITS) and the Minister of Education and Merit, Giuseppe Valditara, who was inaugurating the new laboratories of the ITS Mobility Academy in the city.

On 27 July 2020, around 200 farmers staged a protest action in Maarheeze against the increasing regulation of their activities by the Dutch government, forming the letters #TJB with their tractor pullers.
On 28 January 2021, people protested in Falesti against the Constitutional Court's decision to dismiss a law offering a special status to the Russian language.
On 6 June 2023, SATSE members held a protest before the Munoz Carinanos Hospital in Sevilla (Andalucia) to demand a salary raise and better working conditions.

On 31 May 2024, at the call of FFF, around 50 people participated in a protest in Passau (Bayern) for climate protection and democracy, and to draw attention to the importance of the EU in tackling the climate crisis. The protest was organized as part of FFF's international climate strike to call for an EU-wide phase-out of coal, oil and gas by 2035, and a doubling of investments in renewable energies and climate-neutral industries.
On 13 February 2021, two hundred residents of Kodzha Teppe protested near Varna, demonstrating against the illegal deforestation of nearby pine forest.

On 6 June 2025, citizens gathered in Mramorak village near Kovin to demand accountability for the Novi Sad canopy collapse and observe 16 minutes of silence in remembrance of the victims as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. A concrete mixer driver drove towards the protesting crowd with the local company's truck, hitting one man from the side and almost hitting many others.

On 15 March 2021, musicians protested in front of Spotify headquarters in Madrid - Centro (Madrid), demanding to pay artists more per stream. The Union of Musicians and Allied Workers (UMAW) called the demonstration worldwide.

On 29 May 2024, as part of a national 'No Fake Italy' campaign and at the call of Coldiretti, around 150 farmers with around 6 inflatable boats staged a demonstration at the port of Salerno (Campania) to protest against the arrival in the port of a ship with 40 containers containing tomatoes from China and against the marketing of counterfeit products.

On 26 March 2023, at the call of the action group Stop the Asylum Crisis, a few dozen people staged a peaceful protest in front of a building that was being occupied by asylum seekers in Brussels - Saint-Josse-Ten-Noode, to demand a solution from the Belgian government for the ongoing asylum crisis.
On 8 February 2025, several hundred residents of Cakovec again gathered for a rally, protesting against the ongoing crisis at a local hospital and demanding guarantees of local healthcare.

On 5 March 2026, in the afternoon, between 300 and 600 students and REBELL staged a protest in Rostock (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern) against the reintroduction of the compulsory military service, criticizing the government's focus on military and corporate interests rather than education, carrying banners reading 'No recruiting for dying'. The protest was part of a nationwide school strike called by the School Strike Against Conscription (Schulstreik gegen Wehrpflicht) initiative, focusing on opposition to mandatory service and military buildup.
On 16 May 2021, hundreds of citizens protested in Eibar (Gipuzkoa) to express solidarity with Palestine. Protesters denounced Israeli attacks on Gaza.

On 28 July 2021, people from the Stop Y Bryn Wind Farm group and three Wales' assembly members gathered outside the Senedd Building in Cardiff Bay to protest plans to build the UK's tallest wind farm in south Wales. They were concerned about the site's heritage, loss of outdoor space, and environmental concerns.

On 10 January 2024, unionized truck drivers continued their blockade of the border crossing point with Ukraine in Korczowa. They were condemning allegedly unfair conditions for Ukrainian transport and trade companies and demanded stronger state oversight.
On 3 December 2024, people held a torchlight procession at a mountain peak in Vindafjord Municipality (coded to Olen) to oppose the possible wind power development in the area.
On 24 February 2022, around 1500 people protested at the Atgimimo Square in Klaipeda, Lithuania calling against Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

On 24 September 2018, approximately 30 people protested outside the PSD regional office in Sibiu, condemning the government attacks against the judiciary and the police brutality in the 10 August protests.
On 29 November 2024, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Lund, Skane, to draw attention to overconsumption and to demand action against climate change.

On 13 January 2022, at the call of eight teacher unions (SNUIPP-FSU, SE-UNSA, FEP-CFDT, SNES-FSU, FO, CGT-Education, SNALC, SUD Education), more than 250 people demonstrated in Montargis. They denounced the coronavirus sanitary protocol established in schools by the Ministry of Education.

On 22 March 2025, people took to the streets in Besancon (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte) to protest against fascism. The event was part of a nationwide day of demonstration called by several trade unions and organizations, including CGT, LDH, and La Cimade, coinciding with the International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination, to denounce systemic racism and promote equality and justice.

On 5 January 2025, members of FACTS (Fylde Against Cable Transmission and Substations) gathered at Squires Gate beach in Blackpool (England) to protest a local wind farm project. The proposed development, which would include 107 wind turbines across two farms off the Fylde coast, sparked local opposition, with FACTS raising concerns about the impact on the environment and the consequent closure of St Annes North Beach for up to two years.

On 7 April 2026, parents of students and representatives of the Gros-Rederching-Singling municipality gathered next to the Les Hirondelles school in Gros-Rederching (Grand Est) to protest against the planned closure of a class for the beginning of school 2026-2027.

On 17 May 2022, at the call of the SCRATS - 'Sindicato Central de Regantes del Acueducto Tajo Segura' union, more than 1,000 farmers, politicians (including the PP-affiliated President of the Murcia Region, President of the Provincial Council of Alicante, and Mayor of Alicante), businessmen, and citizens gathered in Alicante (Valencia) against the cutting of the Tagus-Segura transfer and the ruin of the field.
On 24 October 2022, around 300 people, including an AFD elected official, demonstrated in Kothen against inflation, high energy costs, and the current government.

On 15 November 2025, at the call of Climate Alliance (Alianza por el Clima), people protested in Burgos (Castilla y Leon) to demand a just ecological transition, an urgent change to the economic model and effective climate justice measures. Protesters also denounced the dependence on fossil fuels, which exacerbates inequalities and causes heat waves, floods, and fires. The protest coincided with the UN Climate Summit (COP30) in Brazil.

On 17 April 2021, roughly 100 anti-government protesters including supporters of Black Lives Matter, Extinction Rebellion and Reclaim The Streets gathered on Southsea Common in Portsmouth in a show of opposition to the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Bill which proposes to give police more powers to shutdown peaceful protests.

On 12 February 2025, around 100 people, including LDH affiliates and antifascist activists, gathered outside the Court of Justice in Paris (Ile-de-France) to protest against the transfer of antifascist activist 'Gino' to Hungary. 'Gino' had been arrested in France after beating up a neonazi activist in Hungary in 2023.
On 14 May 2021, several hundred people, organized by VND, protested in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, in support of Palestinian people, after the conflict in The Gaza Strip.
On 24 July 2021, the 'Brazilian-German Collective for Democracy' protested in Freiburg im Breisgau against the Brazilian government under Jair Bolsonaro.

On 19 September 2024, artists, cultural workers and local activists gathered for a rally in Lucenec, protesting against what they see as controversial, chaotic and harmful management of the Ministry of culture and other recent actions made by the current government led by the Smer party.
On 31 December 2021, Fridays for Future activists demonstrated in front of the City Hall in Umea to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.

On 2 April 2023, Catholic activists gathered for a march in Augustow, protesting against a recent accusation of the 'Polish pope' John Paul II (Karol Wojtyla) regarding alleged deliberate covering-up of sexual scandals in the church.
On 13 July 2022, several dozen employees of the municipal services of Warsaw and the Solidarity Labour Union representatives gathered for a rally, demanding higher wages.

On 29 March 2025, at the call of the Save Razac and the Cole Valley (Sauvergardons Razac et la Vallee de la Cole) association, around 100 people, including residents and local activists, protested in Thiviers (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) against the construction of a quartz quarry in the locality, highlighting the environmental destruction and the irreversible damage to the local landscape that the quarry would cause.

On 11 May 2023, environmental demonstrated outside of the House of the Estates in Helsinki with the aim to raise awareness about the diminishing forest carbon sinks in Finland and to urge decisive measures against climate change. The protest occurred during ongoing government discussions on climate policy and other topics. Activists from the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation took part in the event.

On 6 June 2020, around 3,000 people protested in Linz under the motto 'Black Lives Matter' against racism and police violence. The protest was sparked by the killing of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.

On 30 May 2023, hundreds of teachers, school employees, and high-school students, protested in Timisoara, demanding better pay for teachers and more investment in the education sector. The USR mayor of Timisoara joined the rally.

On 8 April 2023, members of Animal Rebellion blocked the meat aisle of a supermarket in Canterbury in protest of people eating lamb at Easter. The group is urging both the public and the government to aid farmers in transitioning towards plant-based food systems. The event was part of a coordinated set of demonstrations across the UK.

Around 13 September 2022 (as reported), at the call of NurSind, 13 health workers staged a protest in front of the Nagar Hospital in Pantelleria (Trapani, Sicilia) against the extension of their permanence on the island beyond the terms set in their contracts due to the lack of turnover and shortage of personnel.

On 23 February 2022, in the morning, SIARC school and hospital canteen workers from Corigliano Rossano gathered outside the Provincial Health Agency (ASP) headquarters in Cosenza (Cosenza, Calabria) to protest against alleged delays in the reception of their salaries, denounce a lack of security in kitchens and lament the mediocrity of their service, citing detrimental shortages in the supply of raw materials by their company.
On 27 January 2023, 10 Extinction Rebellion activists glued themselves to the theatre in Bregenz, protesting against the Bodensee speedway project and denouncing the project's environmental impact.

On 28 October 2025, over 300 students from Western Serbia completed their fourth day of march to Novi Sad and spent their night in Koceljeva, where they were welcomed by locals. Their goal is to arrive in Novi Sad by November 1 for a planned protest that marks the anniversary of the concrete canopy collapse at the train station, which resulted in the deaths of 16 people. The march honors the victims and aims to raise awareness about corruption while demanding accountability for the tragedy.

On 13 June 2022, members of the Bristol Feminist Collective gathered outside the Bristol Family Court in Bristol to protest domestic abuse. Demonstrators claimed that judges and magistrates had a poor understanding of domestic abuse and its effect on custody arrangements.
On 3 April 2022, about 700 people marched in Daugavpils, Latvia calling against the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

On 25 February 2023, one year after the outbreak of war in Ukraine, at the call of Europe for Peace and 'Rete Salento per la pace', people took to the streets in Lecce (Lecce, Puglia), from Porta Napoli to Piazza Sant'Oronzo, to protest against the ongoing war and to call on the Italian government to take effective negotiating action to bring the conflict to an end. Demonstrators protested against the sending of weapons. A Russian musician affiliated with 'Akrady Kots' opposing Russia's president took part in the demonstration.

On 17 May 2025, around 250 people, including members and elected officials of BSW, The Greens, The Left, and the voter group GfE, staged a protest in Emden (Niedersachsen) against the planned closure of the 24/7 emergency clinics, criticizing the clinic management for breaking the promise made in a citizens' referendum to maintain emergency care.

On 26 January 2025, citizens held a protest in Bajina Basta in support of students who have been occupying their faculties nationwide, demanding accountability for the loss of 15 lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the train station in Novi Sad, ultimately blaming corruption for this tragic event.
On 13 October 2020, about 150 people gathered outside the Anglican Cathedral in Liverpool for a Black Lives Matter protest.

On 11 March 2021, around 70 private sector health workers and CGT union members protested in Millau to call for more human resources, a bonus, and a monthly salary increase that hospital health workers have been granted by the Segur agreements.

On 24 September 2022, anti-fascist protestors gathered near Parliament Square in London - Westminster to block the route of a far-right protest that was supposed to happen and protest against the government's alleged racism. Some protesters held a banner saying 'refugees welcome'.

On 24 February 2022, citizens of Ukraine residing in Croatia protested in front of the Russian embassy in Zagreb (City of Zagreb) against the war in Ukraine. They were joined by other citizens who showed solidarity with the Ukrainian people. Protesters demanded diplomatic and humanitarian aid from the Croatian government and other European Union member states.
On 10 April 2024, activists gathered for a rally in Michalovce, calling for immediate ceasefire in Ukraine. At least some of them supported the Russian position in the ongoing war.

On 5 April 2023, 4 ALG activists blocked the Neue Kant street in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the street by the police.
On 9 October 2020, Fridays For Future activists staged a protest in Karlstad to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.

On 28 June 2023, overnight, rioters vandalized the Les Resots du Coeur association in Marly, while vandalizing and setting fire to other street furniture and buildings, including a restaurant and a bowling alley. The event was part of a national wave of riots and demonstrations denouncing police violence and demanding justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre on 27 June 2023.

On 17 August 2024, activists, called by the Free Russians Association (Associao de Russos Livres) as a part of a series of weekly protests, held a protest in Lisboa (Lisboa) against Russia's war on Ukraine and demanded the release of political activists prisoners Andrei Gnet and Vladislav Arnichev, as well as showed solidarity with Venezuela.

On 1 April 2021, teachers supported by their federations DOE and OLME and joined by university and school students marched in Athens - Central Athens against the recently passed education law allowing police to patrol university campuses and against the government's handling of the coronavirus pandemic. Another student protest against the education law and demanding the reopening of universities with increased coronavirus safety measures took place the same day.

On 30 October 2024, residents of Donja Jablanica blocked the M-17 highway in protest, expressing their dissatisfaction with the current state of infrastructure in their village. This protest followed the devastating consequences of a recent flood, which was exacerbated by a nearby illegal quarry that collapsed under the rush of water. The residents demanded that local authorities conduct a safety assessment and address the housing issues faced by those affected by the floods.

On 20 November 2020, 100 demonstrators protested in front of the Bulgarian National Television building, demanding resignation Prime Minister Borisov, Prosecutor General Geshev, the Parliament, as well as snap parliamentarian elections.
On 19 August 2021, people protested in Ruggell with cowbells and banners against the coronavirus measures.

On 8 February 2024, around 10 students' parents blocked access to the local school and kept the teachers from exiting the building in Autreches (Hauts-de-France) to protest against the announced closure of classes.

On 21 April 2021, around 200 people protested in Dusseldorf for the release of Russian opposition leader Alexey Navalny and immediate medical treatment for Navalny. The protest was organized by 'Free Russia NRW'.

On 17 July 2025, county-pension-house employees affiliated with National Union Bloc- Blocul National Sindical (BNS) staged a peaceful protest outside the County Pension House in Baia Mare (Maramures), denouncing the Government's austerity package that caps 'hazard' allowances, cuts extra leave and perpetuates pay inequities. Action was part of a BNS-coordinated national series of demonstrations at county pension offices.
On 24 September 2021, students organized by FFF: Fridays for Future gathered in central Tallinn to demand more action by governments in the face of climate change.
On 7 September 2021, an unknown number of activists of the Groen and Vooruit parties staged a protest action in Lint against the imminent cancellation of two De Lijn bus lines in the neighborhood.

On 25 November 2021, people, including feminist collectives, gathered for a human chain in Wurzburg to protest against violence against women and call for equality. Protesters gathered on the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

Around 10 April 2021 (as reported), between 300 and 1,000 no mask activists, among them 3V Movement activists, gathered in Ravenna under the banner 'No Paura Day' (No Fear Day) to protest against the measures taken to stop the spread of coronavirus, considered too strict. The police sanctioned 11 people for not respecting Covid-19 restrictions.

On 8 March 2023, at the call of Non Una di Meno, about 3,000 people took to the streets in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to defend women's and LGBT rights on International Women's Day, denounce the patriarchy, and remember the victims of gender violence. Students' collectives and feminist associations' activists took part in the demonstration.

On 1 March 2023, at the call of Ver.di, around 150 young striking employees of the public sector, including from Stadtwerke Kiel and Lubeck, the Kiel Municipal Hospital, the Helios Clinic in Schleswig and the Forde Sparkasse Kiel, gathered outside the Rathausplatz in Kiel (Schleswig-Holstein, Kiel) to demand higher wages amid inflation.

On 16 June 2020, around 20 health workers and union members gathered in La Roche-sur-Yon, in front of the hospital and in front of the prefecture in La Roche-sur-Yon. They protested as part of the national day of actions for the defense of public hospitals at the call of CFDT, CGT and FO.
On 31 October 2021, library workers in Silistra protested for higher wages, claiming that they deserve more than the minimum wage.
On 3 July 2021, around 1,000 lesbian women gathered for a DYKE March in Koln to protest for more visibility of lesbian women.
Around 5 July 2020, Belarusian citizens protested in Frankfurt am Main for free elections and the release of political prisoners.
On 24 September 2021, around 1900 people protested in Nurnberg at the call of FFF to urge the government to implement concrete measures to tackle climate change.
On 29 September 2020, architects and surveyors gathered in Latina to protest against the delays in the city's technical department.

On 3 August 2024, estimated 150 far-right demonstrators gathered outside Leeds Art Gallery in Leeds (England) for an anti-immigration demonstration. Demonstrators chanted slogans such as 'You're not English anymore' and 'Paedo Muslims off our street'. Around 250 anti-racism and pro-Palestine counter-demonstrators gathered at the same location and chanted 'Say it loud, say it clear, refugees are welcome here' and 'Nazi scum off our streets'. The number of counter protesters grew during the afternoon. Police forces arrested several far-right demonstrators after an unspecified incident on George Street. The event is part of mass anti-migration gatherings and riots occurring across the country after the mass stabbing of children in Southport on 29 July 2024 2024 and the disinformation campaign on social media about the suspect of the attack being a refugee..
On 5 September 2022, around 30 teachers protested in Nyugati square in Budapest - VI, demanding higher wages, more teaching staff, and better working conditions.

On 13 March 2025, at the call of Ver.di, around 1,000 public service employees gathered at Bollwerk and marched to the Market Square, where a rally was held, in Andernach (Rheinland-Pfalz). This rally was part of a broader strike to demand an eight percent wage increase and highlight issues like staff shortages and increased workloads amid the ongoing public service wage negotiations.

On 25 November 2022, an unknown number of Vooruit party members staged a protest in Roeselare to denounce violence against women in the context of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women.

On 6 November 2021, at the call of the local COP26 Coalition branch, around 50 climate activists, as well as members of Limerick Against Pollution and PBP, marched through Limerick (Limerick City and County) to protest, demanding leaders gathered at the COP26 climate conference in Glasgow to take drastic action to counter climate change.

On 19 November 2025, at 9:30 am, around 600 students, teachers, parents, residents, and elected administrators took to the streets in Lecce (Puglia) to demand respect for children's rights and peace for Ukraine and Palestine. The event, held on the International Children's Rights Day, was organized by the mayor and the Department of Education. The regional councilor for public education and representatives of UNICEF participated in the demonstration.

On 26 September 2022, more than 500 people held an LGBT march in La Roche-sur-Yon on the occasion of Diversity week started on 19 September. The march started from Pierre Mendes France, and ended downtown.

Around 11 February 2024, people called by the Liberation of Palestine (Libertacao da Palestina) collective held a protest in Faro (Faro) in solidarity with the Palestinian people and against Israeli violence amid the ongoing war in the Gaza Strip, and to demand a permanent ceasefire and a boycott campaign against Israel.
On 29 November 2025, in the evening, around 300 artists and cultural workers staged a protest in Munchen (Bayern) against increased rents.

On 21 June 2023, university students gathered outside the military hospital in the Baggio neighborhood of Milano - Municipio 7 (Milano, Lombardia) to demand that said infrastructure, which is not fully in use, be turned into a student residence. A municipal councilor (EV) took part in the demonstration.
On 19 September 2020, members of Stand Up To Racism and Care4Calais held a rally in Sheffield as part of a day of action in solidarity with refugees in the UK.

On 27 August 2021, hundreds of climate activists, including Extinction Rebellion and Greenpeace members, staged a protest performance in front of the Parliament of Norway (Stortinget) in Oslo to demand the declaration of climate emergency and to draw attention to climate crisis.

On 5 March 2026, at the call of SNES-FSU, teachers picketed at their school in Lille (Hauts-de-France). The event was part of a nationwide demonstration by teachers against the impacts of the austerity budget imposed on the French Ministry of National Education, including the axing of teaching positions in the national education system, the reduced allocation of teaching hours and the elimination of classes at the start of the new school year.

On 27 July 2020, women of Molyvos (Mithymna) held a rally demanding NGOs leave and protesting against renting hotels to host migrants. This protest took place following rumours that rooms were to be rented to asylum seekers. The Migration Ministry has denied the rumours, but the financial strain because of the coronavirus pandemic is refuelling tension over migration.

Around 4 March 2020 (as reported), around 500 students and teachers from the art department of the Atlascollege staged a protest action in the Molenvijverpark in Genk against the budget cuts in the cultural sector by the Flemish Government, by floating pieces of art on the park pond.

On 4 December 2021, campaigners for refugee rights gathered in Consett to demonstrate in opposition to plans to use a nearby facility in Hassockfield to house detained female refugees. The protest was organised by Durham People's Assembly and No to Hassockfield with members of Women for Refugee Women and the Feminist Theatre Group present.

On 20 September 2024, women, including representatives of Women's Network of Croatia, protested in front of the Ministry of Health in Zagreb, demanding resignation of the Minister and all others responsible for allowing a gynaecologist in Osijek to continue working even after being accused of committing sexual violence which allowed him to repeat the crime. They also demanded changes in laws to suspend doctors who are accused of committing sexual violence, such as rape. Women's organizations organized symbolic actions with the message 'Stop protecting rapists' in 17 Croatian cities and towns on the same day.

On 26 January 2026, transport operators, long-range bus and transport companies and smaller transporters protested by blocking truck traffic in Novo Selo. They demanded changes to the European Union entry and exit system to address restrictions on professional drivers' length of stay in the Schengen area. The protests were held across all the main border crossings in the country and lasted for several days.

On 15 June 2025, in the afternoon, dozens of residents gathered in Brasschaat (Vlaanderen), hanging banners throughout the area to protest the subdivision of green spaces and tree removal for new social housing projects.
On 30 December 2020, around 100 demonstrators gathered in front of a local police station and later moved to the central area of Eksjo over the recent fatal shooting and against police violence.

On 6 June 2020, a small group of protesters gathered in Ballinamore, Co. Leitrim to stage a silent protest to support the Black Lives Matter movement and call for justice for George Floyd, an unarmed black man killed by a police officer in the United States.

On 14 June 2025, over 1,000 people gathered on Groenplaats Square in Antwerpen (Vlaanderen) in support of Palestine and to demand an end to the ongoing violence in Gaza. They called on governments and companies to sever their ties with Israel, signaling that a red line had been crossed by the country.

On 1 September 2020, Extinction Rebellion members staged a 'die-in' outside the Department for Work and Pensions office and marched around St Peter's Square in Manchester as part of the nationwide activism to raise awareness of climate change.

On 23 July 2025, citizens gathered in Vranje, protesting against the ruling regime, demanding extraordinary parliamentary elections, and condemning the police brutality towards peacefully protesting students.

On 2 September 2023, people took part in the 'Stroller March' in Halmstad, Halland, to raise awareness of the problem of maternal mortality. The demonstration was a part of a nationwide campaign held on 2 and 3 September 2023 and was organized by the Swedish Association for Sexuality Education (RFSU).

On 29 November 2024, citizens gathered in Sremski Karlovci to pause all their activities for 15 minutes as part of the 'Serbia, stop' campaign. During their protest action, a group of officials and activists from the ruling SNS political party attempted to disperse the protesters who were blocking the road in front of the Karlovci high school. This initiative aimed to demand accountability from the authorities while honoring the 15 victims of the Novi Sad tragedy, which occurred when a concrete canopy collapsed at the city's railway station.

On 28 February 2024, farmers continued blocking a border crossing point between Poland and Ukraine near Medyka, protesting against ongoing imports of Ukrainian grains to the EU and demanding higher support to the national agriculture.
